review.summary: Riding already looks and sounds like Bangkok: 14 Thai bike kinds drawn at true size, a rigged rider and pillion, bikes parked at the kerb, the engine noise that draws zombies, and the headlight trade-off at night. The awkward feel does not come from the speed numbers. It has three root causes. (1) What you see does not match where the bike goes. The bike is always drawn in one of 3 straight-on views, so every keyboard diagonal (always exactly 45 degrees) looks like the bike is sliding sideways, and the side-view 'lean' looks like a wheelie. At the default zoom you see only about 0.4 s of road ahead when riding north or south. (2) Hitting things has no real consequence. The bike collides like a person on foot (a 10x4 px box for a bike drawn 31 px long), so its front wheel sinks into walls, it slides along walls without damage, and it rides straight through parked bikes, kerbs, road medians and bodies. You are never thrown off: riding into 21 zombies at full speed only slows you to a crawl. A grabbed rider can also ride away and still gets bitten 275 px later. (3) The rider's key moments take no time at all: getting on, stopping from 60 km/h and hopping off, and sitting at a standstill with both feet still on the pegs. Recommended direction: keep the speeds, sizes and the 4 views, and change the rule to 'fast and safe on the open road, fragile and loud when you hit something'. Do it in three steps. First, draw and frame the bike by its real heading: skew the side view to the heading, point the headlight where the bike goes, and zoom out with speed. Second, give contact consequences using systems that already exist: a collision check at the front wheel, scraping, bumps from kerbs and bodies, parked bikes that fall over, being thrown off with the existing side-view fall plus a dropped bike, and zombies that can pull you off. Third, give the rider low-risk actions instead of weapons: a brake, quiet coasting, a horn to lure zombies, a start-up delay, a foot down when stopped, and pushing the bike home into the shophouse.
strengths: The 14 bike models are real Thai street kinds at true proportions (about 1.9 m, 31 px side-on), each with its own colours, plus delivery boxes, a motorbike-taxi rider's orange vest and a basket. All makes are invented (คาเซะ/โทระ/ไรจิน/โวลต้า/เวลโล่/บริตตัน), so the no-brands rule holds (bike_art.gd:16-33, 193-205; data/vehicles.cfg).

The rider sits between the bike's far and near parts, on per-model seat, handlebar and footpeg anchors, and the rig leans the body forward until the hands reach the bars (bike_art.gd:39-54, rig.gd:351-372). The pillion holds the rider's waist and frees their arms to fight (player.gd:566-581). 'One rides, one fights' is a good co-op rule, so keep fighting pillion-only (main.gd:566).

The engine works as a lure. Its noise carries 180-420 px while zombies see only 120 px by day and 55 px in the dark, and the headlight makes you visible at night (vehicles.gd:201-204, zombie.gd:71-72, 520). Parking the bike at home draws zombies to your door. These are real trade-offs and should stay.

Bikes are parked the Bangkok way: nose to the road along the kerb, in rows, never across a shop front or a door, nose-in along sois (city_gen.gd:925-1070), and a test enforces it (tests/test_vehicles.gd:43-51).

The small details are alive and cheap: the brake light, a scuff mark on the tyre that rolls round, exhaust puffs on the throttle, dust on hard turns, bobbing on the road, a synthesized single-cylinder engine whose pitch follows speed, an electric whine, and screen shake on crashes (bike_art.gd:325-363, player.gd:535-675, sfx.gd:109-125).

The access rules feel real: 35% of bikes still have the key in, you hotwire the rest with a screwdriver held in hand in 8 s, fuel and battery run out, and a jerrycan refills petrol bikes (vehicles.gd:16-20, 321-365).

The code base is sound. The server decides everything, and the same Vehicles.step runs on the server and for the rider's own prediction. Only bikes that changed are saved. tests/test_vehicles.gd covers riding, pillion, steering, crashes, doors, hotwiring and reloads.
The speedometer panel reads cleanly (km/h, a rev bar, fuel bars, model name, E to get off) and slides in. The camera already looks ahead in the direction you ride (bike_dash.gd, main.gd:1029-1037).

findings.title: Nothing ever knocks you off the bike
findings.observation: Crashes, crowds and bumps only cost speed and bike HP; the rider never leaves the seat unless the bike breaks. Measured (ride_shots.gd, seed 11): full throttle (150 px/s) into a 3x7 block of 21 normal zombies: speed 150 -> 92 -> 44 -> 13 px/s within ~0.3 s, 9 knocked flat, bike HP 60 -> 33 in 0.6 s, then the bike keeps inching through them at 20-50 px/s (zombies are shoved aside); the rider never fell and was never grabbed. Wall at 150 px/s: HP 60 -> 54 and a bruise, still seated. Zombies already lying down are skipped entirely (you ride over them with no effect).
findings.evidence: scripts/vehicles.gd:206-226 (per zombie: knock_down, v.hp -= 3, ride_vel *= 0.6; dismount only when hp <= 0); vehicles.gd:210 (down_t > 0 -> continue); vehicles.gd:230-243 (_crash = dent + bruise only); tests/test_vehicles.gd:224 ('but you stay on (it's not that hard a game)'); main.gd:651-655 (zombies are pushed off players; a player is never blocked by bodies); ROADMAP.md:229 ('ต่อไป: ชนแรงจนตกรถ'). Screenshot life/ride_r5_crowd_after_z4.png: centre of the image, the rider is invisible inside the crowd, only damage numbers show.
findings.why: A bike should be the fastest and most fragile way to move: the fear is 'one mistake and I am on the ground next to them'. Now the worst case is a slow crawl, so riding has no near-death moment (the ROADMAP's 'เฉียดตาย' fun) and the bike is simply safer than walking. Real riders fall when they hit a body, a kerb or a wall at speed.
findings.suggestion: Add a 'thrown off' outcome to Vehicles. Triggers (per-model thresholds, see ride-09): a wall or car hit above CRASH (125 px/s); hitting a fat zombie above HIT_SPEED; 3 or more zombie hits within 1 s; riding over a downed body above ~110 px/s (a chance). Result: dismount, and fling the rider 16-28 px along the heading (World.slide). Draw it with the side-view fall zombies already use for knock-downs (Look st.fall + fall_dir, zombie.gd:856), then getup_t ~1.2 s through the existing stand-up path, Body.add bruise or graze, 5-15 HP. The bike falls over (v.upright = false: already stored and saved, never used), slides ~1 cell, and the engine stalls. The player stands it up with an E action 'ยกรถ' (1 s) before riding again. The crash noise (160 px) already exists. Keep low-speed contact forgiving (below HIT_SPEED you push, you don't fall), so the risk comes from speed in crowds, not from riding itself.
findings.scope_check: Uses existing views: the fall is side-view only, which the scope allows for falls and lying poses (fall = green, lying/low = yellow, side view only). The fallen bike is the existing side art laid flat, no new character view. Mostly system work plus one transform. Per frame: nothing extra (it is a one-off event).

findings.title: Diagonal riding looks like sliding sideways (the bike snaps to 3 fixed views)
findings.observation: The bike picks side, front or back from its heading using the character rule: it stays in side view while |cos| > 0.55 (up to ~56 degrees), and stays in front or back view until |cos| > 0.85. It is always drawn straight-on. Keyboard steering only gives 0, 45 or 90 degrees, so every diagonal is exactly 45 degrees, the worst case. Coming from east-west riding you get a level side-on bike moving 45 degrees down the screen (ride_r1: logged velocity (106,106), bike drawn level). Coming from north-south riding you get a bike facing the camera while it moves 45 degrees sideways (ride_r2). The side-view 'lean' is a rotation in the screen plane driven by turn rate (±0.2 rad), so mid-turn it reads as a wheelie or nose-dive, and it goes back to level while you are still riding diagonally. The headlight beam also snaps to 4 directions: in ride_r2 the beam cone points straight down while the bike goes south-east. Seen end-on (DEPTH 0.35) the 1.9 m bike is only ~7 px deep, a sliver under the rider (v02/v03/v05), while parked cars running north-south are drawn about 3 cells long (v05, v11). The view change is a paper-thin flip (ride_r7, squash down to 0.18).
findings.evidence: scripts/look.gd:62-67 (pick_view thresholds); vehicles.gd:147-154 (turn_to); player.gd:539 (xf = Transform2D(lean, squash...) in every view); player.gd:660-675 (lean from turn rate); player.gd:595-598 (headlight rotation from view/dir only); main.gd:967-970 (8-way input); bike_art.gd:69 (DEPTH 0.35). Screenshots: life/ride_r1_diag_side_z4.png (rider centre), life/ride_r2_diag_front_night_z4.png (beam straight down from the bike at centre), life/ride_r7_midturn_z5.png (rider squashed thin at top centre), life/v02_ride_soi_front_z4.png.
findings.why: The eye reads a bike's direction from its long axis. A bike moving where it isn't pointing looks like it is on ice, and in motion this is the most visibly 'off' thing. Characters get away with 4 views because a person is round; a 1.9 m bike is a long arrow.
findings.suggestion: Keep the 4 views but draw them by the real heading. (a) Side view: replace the rotation lean with a skew from the smoothed heading h (ride_seen, which every machine already has). Set xf's x-axis to (|cos h|, sin h * sign(cos h) * K) and its y-axis to (0,1), with K = BikeArt.DEPTH. The wheels then follow the ground line, vertical parts stay vertical, and at the view switch the side view is already shortened toward the front-view shape. The rider is drawn under Look.body_xf, so the hands stay on the bars. (b) Front/back view: BikeArt already draws the 'far' and 'near' parts separately, so shift far by -Δ and near by +Δ (Δ ≈ 10 * sin of the angle away from vertical) so the wheelbase points the way you go. Keep the rotation lean in these views, where it correctly reads as roll. (c) Headlight rotation = ride_seen.angle(). (d) Raise BikeArt.DEPTH to ~0.5 so the bike has a visible length end-on (one constant; the rider anchors follow it, so check the hands visually). (e) Once the skew hides the jump, move the view switch to ~45 degrees with hysteresis and set the minimum squash to ~0.5.
findings.scope_check: No new views or clothing templates: it is a transform on existing art, and the rider follows through Look.body_xf. Per frame: one Transform2D per ridden bike, which is already redrawn every frame. Art transform only, no new art.

findings.title: You can barely see ahead when riding north or south
findings.observation: Default zoom 4 in the 1280x720 window shows 320x180 world px. The camera looks ahead by 0.3 s of speed, capped at 48 px. Riding south at 150 px/s (ride_r6, HUD on): the rider's feet are at y≈310 of 720, and the speedometer panel (y 543-615, bottom centre) plus the faded hotbar cover the bottom of the screen. That leaves ~58 world px (~3.6 cells, 0.39 s) of clear road ahead, and 0.23 s on the 250 px/s sports bike. Riding east you get 160+48 = 208 px (1.4 s). Riding north, tall 3/4-view roofs and the BTS deck hide the road ahead (known from the city review).
findings.evidence: scripts/main.gd:107-108 (CAM_LEAD 0.3, CAM_LEAD_MAX 48); main.gd:1029-1037; bike_dash.gd:28-31 (bottom centre, 74 px tall); ui.gd:509 (hotbar only faded to alpha 0.18); main.gd:1199 (a zoom-out already exists for roofs: play_zoom * lerp(1, 0.78, roof_k)). Screenshot life/ride_r6_fast_south_hud_z4.png (rider at upper centre, speedometer panel at lower centre over the road ahead).
findings.why: Reaction time, not top speed, is what makes a vehicle feel controllable. With under half a second, obstacles appear already under the wheel, so players either crawl everywhere or crash into things they never saw, and both read as 'the bike handles badly'. GTA 1/2 solved this by zooming out with speed.
findings.suggestion: (1) Link zoom-out to speed using the existing roof mechanism: want = play_zoom * lerp(1, 0.78, roof_k) * lerp(1.0, 0.75, ride_k), with ride_k = ride_spd/150 smoothed over ~1 s (zoom 4 -> 3 at full speed). (2) While riding, raise CAM_LEAD_MAX from 48 to ~80 and multiply the look-ahead by ~1.4 vertically, since the screen is shortest there. (3) While riding, hide the hotbar completely (the rider can't use it) and put a compact speedometer panel (speed + fuel) in its slot or at the bottom right, so the bottom centre shows road. Result: ~190 px (~1.3 s) of road ahead riding south, about 3x today.
findings.scope_check: Zoom only, no camera angle or rotation (the 1-6 zoom range already exists, and so does the roof zoom-out). The HUD gets cleaner, not busier. Zoom 3 shows 1.8x the ground, so check web fps with ?perf while riding past zombies.

findings.title: The bike collides like a pedestrian: wheel in the wall, walls act as rails, the street is flat
findings.observation: The ridden bike uses RADIUS 5, the same 10x4 px foot box as a person, while it is drawn ~31 px long side-on. Measured: riding east into a wall, the bike's centre stops 5 px short and the drawn front wheel ends 10.5 px inside the wall (ride_r9). Steering 45 degrees into a shop front at 150 px/s, the bike slid along it at 109 px/s with ride_vel still 150 and no damage (a 'wall rail'): a hit only counts when the bike moved less than 50% of its step. Parked motorbikes are not solid, so you ride through rows of them. Road-to-pavement kerbs, raised medians (drawn raised, but the tiles are plain ROAD) and downed zombies have no effect. 1 in 7 parked bikes is generated as fallen over (upright = false) but is drawn standing.
findings.evidence: scripts/vehicles.gd:15, 112-115; world.gd:872-877 (_feet: box depth r*0.4) and 780-812 (slide); city_gen.gd:1092-1095 (_bike_box: the generator already knows a parked bike is 34x8 side-on and 12x16 end-on); city_gen.gd:1089-1090 (_park adds no blocked cell); city_gen.gd:191-196 (medians are only a list of rectangles); vehicles.gd:70 and street_prop.gd:388-389 (upright is never drawn); vehicles.gd:210. Screenshot life/ride_r9_wall_nose_z5.png: the front wheel overlaps the cream wall band right of x≈570 (partly under a faded roof).
findings.why: What makes a Bangkok street feel real on two wheels is its physical texture: rows of parked bikes to thread through, kerbs you slow for, a median you can't cross, walls you scrape. Right now the street is a flat ice rink and the front wheel sinks into walls.
findings.suggestion: All changes in Vehicles.step. (a) Front check: also test can_stand(pos + heading*13, 3, road) and count a block as a hit, so the front wheel meets the wall, not the rider's hips. (b) Scrape: when the bike moves between 50% and 95% of its intended step, set ride_vel to the velocity it actually moved (dropping the part into the wall), add a jolt, scrape sparks and sound, and v.hp -1 per ~0.5 s. (c) Kerb: crossing ROAD/SOI to SIDEWALK or back above ~90 px/s multiplies ride_vel by 0.75, with a jolt of 1.5 and dust. (d) Parked bikes: a riderless bike within 10 px of the front wheel above HIT_SPEED is knocked over (upright=false, NOISE_HIT, both bikes lose HP, ride_vel *= 0.5), so rows can topple like dominoes. People on foot still walk through. (e) Medians: at run time, treat cells in w.medians as solid for riders only, with gaps every ~40 cells and at junctions ('จุดกลับรถ'). This needs no GEN bump. (f) Riding over a downed zombie: a jolt, stomp damage, and a chance to fall at speed (ride-01). Draw a fallen bike as the side art laid flat (y scaled ~0.5 about its centre, flat shadow) in StreetProp._motorbike.
findings.scope_check: System and data, and each part is S on its own. The fallen bike is a transform of existing art; no new views. Per frame: one extra can_stand plus a short scan of nearby bikes, for riders only. The median change needs no city regeneration.

findings.title: Getting on, stopping and getting off take no time
findings.observation: Pressing E next to a bike snaps you up to 22 px onto it and you can ride that same frame. The sound is the 'door' thump (a fist and shoulder against wood). E at any speed, even 180 px/s, dismounts instantly: ride_vel = 0, the bike stops dead where it is, and you appear 9 px south of it (the first free spot; in front or back view that is in front of or behind the wheel). When stopped, both rider and pillion keep their feet on the pegs (ride_r8: speed 0): no foot down, no kickstand.
findings.evidence: scripts/vehicles.gd:252-263 (mount: position = v.pos; fx_sound 'door'); actions.gd:15-16 (E while riding -> dismount); vehicles.gd:282-314 (dismount/_step_off: velocity zeroed, (0,9) tried first); player.gd:543 + bike_art.gd:105-113 (feet always on the pegs); sfx.gd:248 ('door': fist and shoulder against wood); audio/WANTED.md:120 (moto_start already wanted). Screenshot life/ride_r8_stopped_pillion_z5.png (centre: both riders stopped, feet up).
findings.why: These three moments are where you see the rider as a person. A Bangkok rider at a stop puts a foot down, brakes before hopping off, and starting a bike takes a second and makes noise. Instant transitions make the bike feel like a costume rather than a machine, and the instant stop-and-hop removes the risk of arriving somewhere dangerous at speed.
findings.suggestion: (1) E while moving above CRAWL brakes the bike to a stop automatically, then you step off (toast 'จอดก่อน'). Step off to the bike's side: (0,±9) in side view, (±10,0) in front/back views. (2) Start-up: add a per-model 'start' time in vehicles.cfg (electric start 0.4 s; kick-start models cub/trail/enfield ~1 s, with a right-leg kick through the rider's foot anchor), a start sound (moto_start) and a noise burst (~NOISE_HIT). A badly damaged bike (HP < 30%) may need a second try. (3) Foot down: when ride_spd < ~8 px/s, move the near foot anchor to the ground beside the peg (side view (pegs.x+2, 0); front/back (±5, 0)) and tilt the bike ~4 degrees toward it in front/back views. Below CRAWL, alternate the feet (paddling along a soi). (4) Replace the mount 'door' sound with a seat or kickstand clack.
findings.scope_check: Anchors only (Rig._anchored already takes feet anchors), no new views. New columns in vehicles.cfg. No per-frame cost.

findings.title: Bug: a grabbed rider rides away and is bitten from 275 px
findings.observation: Measured with a stopped bike and a zombie 10 px away with grab chance 1: grabbed after 0.45 s. Riding off at full throttle still worked while held. 2.2 s later (GRAB_TIME) the bite landed with the rider 275 px from the zombie, moving at 150 px/s (HP 100 -> 89). Zombies can't pull a rider off.
findings.evidence: scripts/vehicles.gd:172-186 (server_tick moves the bike whatever grabbed_by is); main.gd:1019-1021 (the client prediction does the same); zombie.gd:346-357 (_hold never checks distance); zombie.gd:186-192 (lunge -> grab); player.gd:297-302 (on foot a grab freezes you; riding skips that check). Output from ride_shots.gd: 'GRAB bitten while riding, 275 px from the zombie, 2.2 s after riding off, speed 150'.
findings.why: The grab rule breaks both ways: the grab doesn't hold you, yet the bite still lands from the far end of the street, which will feel like a random, unfair hit. It is also exactly the genre's key scene, a crowd closing round a stalled bike, and right now it can't happen.
findings.suggestion: While grabbed_by >= 0, ignore the throttle (brake to 0) in Vehicles.server_tick and in the client prediction. If the grab happens above ~30 px/s, the rider is dragged off using ride-01's thrown-off path, falling toward the zombie. Struggling (Space or clicks) works as now and frees you to ride on. In Zombie._hold, release the grab if the victim is more than ~20 px away, as a safety net for any other moving case. Add the case to test_vehicles.
findings.scope_check: System only; no art, views or per-frame cost.

findings.title: One pedal, free corners, and the rider's buttons do nothing
findings.observation: With no input the bike brakes at 1.6x accel (wave: 272 px/s²; 150 -> 0 in 0.55 s over ~41 px, i.e. from 60 km/h on the speedometer to zero in under 3 m). There is no coasting and no brake key; you brake by letting go or by steering back more than 132 degrees. Corners cost nothing: at top speed the wave turns at 3.2 rad/s (radius ~47 px, about 3 cells) and keeps full speed, so you can turn 90 degrees into a 3-cell soi flat out and at worst slide along the wall (ride-04). Engine noise follows speed (0.5 + 0.5*speed/top), not the throttle. While riding, the left/right mouse buttons and Space do nothing, because fighting is pillion-only.
findings.evidence: scripts/vehicles.gd:93-109 (letting go = brake 1.6x accel; turning never loses speed); vehicles.gd:24-27; vehicles.gd:201-204 (noise from speed); main.gd:566 (the rider can't attack, so those inputs are free); ROADMAP.md:197 ('บีบแตร'); audio/WANTED.md:122 (moto_horn, 'ยังไม่มีปุ่ม').
findings.why: Real riding is throttle, brake and cornering: you slow down for a corner and roll off the gas into your soi. With one pedal and free corners there is no riding skill, only steering around things. And the loud-versus-quiet choice, which is what makes a bike interesting in a game about noise and stealth, isn't available.
findings.suggestion: (1) Letting go = engine braking at ~0.5x accel (you coast ~1.5 s). Space (free while riding) = brakes at 1.6x accel, with the brake light and skid dust. Keep braking by steering back. (2) Grip-limited turning: max turn rate = GRIP / speed (e.g. GRIP 420 px/s², giving 2.8 rad/s at 150). Steering harder than that scrubs off speed with skid dust, so corners slow you down naturally. (3) Noise from the throttle: noise = m.noise * (0.35 + 0.65 * throttle). Coasting into your soi at night is quieter; revving is loud. (4) Left click = horn (noise ~300 px, 1 s cooldown): a lure you sound before riding off. The rider's one 'combat' action stays a risk tool, and fighting stays the pillion's job. (5) Optional setting 'mouse steer' (W = throttle, the bike heads toward the cursor) for smooth curves like the Victory Monument roundabout.
findings.scope_check: System and data; the horn goes through Main.stimulus. No new art (brake light, dust and puffs already exist). No per-frame cost.

findings.title: Push your bike home and park it inside, like every shophouse does
findings.observation: A bike can only be ridden (engine on, noisy) or left behind. Riding is barred from FLOOR and DOOR tiles, so a bike can never enter a building. An empty tank means abandoning the bike. In real Bangkok shophouse life, the family's bikes are wheeled into the shop front at night and the rolling shutter comes down, and 'เข็นรถ' (pushing a bike) when out of fuel is an everyday sight.
findings.evidence: scripts/world.gd:889-890 (the road flag forbids FLOOR/DOOR); tests/test_vehicles.gd:233-255 ('a bike can't go in through a door'); data/prefabs README (shop downstairs, rolling shutters); ROADMAP.md:197 (furniture dragging and body dragging planned: 'ลากเฟอร์นิเจอร์', 'ค้น/ลากศพ'); ROADMAP.md:126 (core rule 7: ownership and rights also cover vehicles); ROADMAP.md:340-341 (claiming a home).
findings.why: It joins the two halves of the user's question. The bike becomes part of 'my home' (parked behind my shutter); running dry becomes a situation (push it home quietly) instead of a dead end; and pushing with the engine off becomes the stealthy way to move a bike through zombie streets.
findings.suggestion: Add an E-wheel action 'เข็นรถ': you walk beside the bike at 0.65x walking speed, with walking noise only and no running, steering the way you walk. It can pass through open doors and shutters onto ground-floor rooms (storey 0, not stairs), and a bike parked inside keeps its position (already saved). Needs one new rig pose, 'walk holding something' (hands anchored, legs walking), which is later reused for the planned furniture and body dragging. Draw the bike beside the walker with the existing three bike views (offset ±8 px sideways in front/back). Later, with home claiming, a bike inside a claimed home counts as yours (core rule 7).
findings.scope_check: The 4 existing views. One new rig pose (goes through the rig, so clothes follow) shared by three planned features. No base building: it uses existing rooms. Per frame: the same cost as a ridden bike.

findings.title: All 14 bikes handle the same
findings.observation: Models differ only in speed (145-250), acceleration (165-280), fuel, noise, HP and off-road. Steering (TURN_SLOW/FAST, CRAWL, U_TURN), braking (1.6x accel) and the bump/crash limits are shared constants. So a 350 cc touring scooter threads a soi exactly like a 110 cc underbone, and a 650 cc sports bike turns like a classic step-through at the same fraction of its top speed.
findings.evidence: data/vehicles.cfg:8-16 (the columns); scripts/vehicles.gd:21-31 (shared handling constants); vehicles.gd:106.
findings.why: In Thailand you choose a bike for where you ride: nimble underbones and step-throughs for sois and pavements, big scooters for avenues, trail bikes for rough ground. If bikes differ only in top speed there is always one 'best' bike, and the city's streets play no part in the choice.
findings.suggestion: Add optional columns with defaults: turn (multiplies TURN_SLOW/FAST), grip (ride-07), brake, weight (pushing through crowds and the fall threshold, ride-01), start/kick (ride-05), clearance (kerb and body bumps, ride-04). Examples: wave/cub turn 1.2; pcx/nmax/forza turn 0.8, brake 1.2 (ABS), weight 1.3; sport turn 0.7, grip 0.8, falls easily; trail high clearance (kerbs and bodies don't bump it). Show a one-line character in the speedometer panel title (e.g. 'คล่อง ซอย').
findings.scope_check: Pure data plus reading it in step(). No art, no views, no per-frame cost.

findings.title: Hitting a zombie gives the wrong feedback
findings.observation: The damage number shows the zombie's remaining HP, not the damage dealt: a hit at 150 px/s does 22.5 damage to a 60 HP zombie but shows '37'. The 'kick' sound plays twice. A kill by the bike uses the 'stomp' death, which turns into a crushed head, instead of the existing 'flung' death. Crashing into a parked car or taxi never sets off its alarm, though a zombie banging on it can.
findings.evidence: scripts/vehicles.gd:215 (passes z.hp as the damage value) vs combat.gd:737-740 (shown as the number); vehicles.gd:216 + combat.gd:753 (two kick sounds); vehicles.gd:218 + combat.gd:503-504 ('stomp' -> 'crush'); corpse.gd:84 and rig.gd:36 (the 'flung' style exists); actions.gd:61-75 (alarm chance only from bang_car). Screenshot life/ride_r5_crowd_after_z4.png: the stacked 50/45/37 numbers above the crowd are remaining HP.
findings.why: Hit feedback is where speed turns into weight: a body thrown along the road, the right number, one thud. Wrong numbers and a head-crush death make the impact read like a stomp at walking pace.
findings.suggestion: Pass speed*0.15 as the damage. Drop the extra 'kick' sound (or play 'crash' at high speed). Call _kill_zombie with style 'flung' when speed > 100, falling along the bike's heading. In _crash, if the thing hit is a parked car or taxi, run the bang_car alarm logic (25%) and dent it.
findings.scope_check: Existing death styles and sounds; no art.

findings.title: Fuel only matters for the first ride
findings.observation: A found bike has 30% fuel on average (fuel * h * 0.6). A wave's 1.2 L lasts 100 s at full throttle, ~15,000 px or about 2.3 crossings of the 400-cell zone. One 3 L jerrycan adds 250 s, about 6 crossings; jerrycans are 'uncommon' loot in tool and general stores. The electric bike can never be recharged. 35% of bikes have the key, and a common screwdriver hotwires the rest in 8 s. Changing zone always dismounts you and leaves the bike behind.
findings.evidence: scripts/vehicles.gd:17, 20, 68-70; data/vehicles.cfg:21-23 (wave: fuel 4, use 0.012); data/items.cfg:781-788 (fuelcan) and 790-795 (screwdriver, common); vehicles.gd:329-341 (refuelling is petrol-only); main.gd:439, 445 (dismount when changing zone); ROADMAP.md:229 ('ดูดน้ำมันจากซากรถ' is next); ROADMAP.md:179 (motorbike-taxi rider zombie planned).
findings.why: Fuel is what links the bike to the core loop (go out, find, use, go again). After the first jerrycan it stops being a decision. Fuel is also where the city can feel Thai: bottled roadside petrol and coin-operated pumps are part of every soi.
findings.suggestion: Keep consumption as it is, and add Thai fuel sources placed in the city. (1) Racks of glass-bottle petrol in front of shophouses and stalls ('น้ำมันขวด', 0.7-1 L per bottle, a few per rack; a Thing or prop with state). (2) Coin-operated fuel pumps ('ตู้น้ำมันหยอดเหรียญ') that need building power (building power already exists). (3) Siphoning from cars and wrecks with a hose (already planned), slow and noisy. (4) Charging the electric bike overnight at home from a running generator (the generator Thing already exists). Keys: the planned motorbike-taxi rider zombie drops the key to a bike at its taxi stand. Later, consider letting a bike travel with you through a zone exit.
findings.scope_check: Data plus Things plus small props (a bottle rack is a few rectangles). No character views.

findings.title: Online, other players' bikes will look jumpy and your own will feel mushy
findings.observation: Other players' bikes skip the smoothing that walkers use (NetCodec.sample_at, showing others 0.12 s in the past). Instead they chase the latest position at 15/s, and snapshots for other players arrive every other tick (10 per second). At 150 px/s the target jumps ~15 px each time, so remote bikes surge and settle, and their lean, wheel and dust (worked out from on-screen movement) jitter. Your own bike is predicted by Vehicles.step, but every frame it is pulled toward the server's position at 2/s, and that position is about one round trip old. So while cruising, what you see drifts to the server's delayed position, and after a stop the bike is pulled forward by speed x round-trip time (~15 px at 100 ms). Not measured with real latency: I only ran the host.
findings.evidence: scripts/player.gd:840-844 (riders skip sample_at); player.gd:835-839 (pull toward net_pos at 2.0*delta, snap beyond 120 px); net.gd:377 (other players every other snapshot); net.gd:425-431; net_codec.gd:173 (INTERP 0.12).
findings.why: A bike is the fastest thing on screen, so any smoothing error shows about 3x more than on a walker. A friend riding beside you will stutter, and your own bike will feel mushy online even though it is perfect when you host.
findings.suggestion: Check first with 2 clients over a tunnel. Then: smooth other players' bikes with sample_at like walkers, and take turn_to and lean from that smoothed velocity. For your own bike, keep a short history of predicted positions with timestamps, and correct only the difference between the server's position and the prediction from one round trip ago, instead of pulling toward the server's position.
findings.scope_check: Network code only; no art or views.

findings.title: Keep the speeds and sizes; fix the view and the contact instead
findings.observation: Walking is 55 px/s, sprinting ~95, bikes 145-250. The speedometer shows 0.4 km/h per px/s (a wave tops out at 60 km/h). Crossing the 400-cell zone takes 116 s walking, 67 s sprinting, 43 s on a wave and 26 s on the sports bike. On screen at zoom 4, a wave crosses the 1280 px window in ~2.1 s. Accelerating 0 to top speed takes 0.7-0.9 s. The bike is drawn at human scale (1.9 m, 31 px), while parked cars are squeezed to ~3.1-3.4 cells (real 4.5-5.3 m), so bike:car is about 0.6 against a real 0.4. With the 240 s day, 43 s of riding is 4.3 game hours (the known clock issue).
findings.evidence: scripts/player.gd:6; data/vehicles.cfg; bike_dash.gd:9; main.gd:10; screenshots life/ride_r8_stopped_pillion_z5.png and life/12_ratchawithi (sedan and pickup next to the bike).
findings.why: The awkward feel is not the numbers: on screen the bike already feels fast. It comes from seeing too little (ride-03) and hitting nothing (ride-01, ride-04). Making bikes faster would make ride-03 worse, and shrinking them would break the rider rig.
findings.suggestion: Leave speed and acceleration as they are, and keep bikes at human scale (they carry a rigged human). When cars become drivable, keep them at their squeezed size and accept the ratio. The only number worth changing is the game clock (known issue): by bike, 'get home before dark' should take seconds, not hours.
findings.scope_check: No change: this protects the rig and view rules.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed in code. In vehicles.gd:206-226, each zombie in the way gets knock_down(), z.hp -= speed*0.15, v.hp -= 3 and ride_vel *= 0.6, and the rider only leaves the bike when v.hp <= 0 (dismount at :223-226). Line :210 skips zombies with down_t > 0, so you ride over bodies with no effect. _crash (:230-243) only dents and bruises. tests/test_vehicles.gd:224 asserts 'but you stay on (it's not that hard a game)'. main.gd:651-655 shoves zombies off players, so the bike always inches through a crowd. v.upright is stored and saved but never used. The pieces for a fall already exist on the player: the fall pose (death path, player.gd:956), the rise pose, getup_t (player.gd:131, 313, 695) and stand_up. I could not re-run the crowd numbers because the crowd section of ride_shots.gd in the scratchpad was overwritten, but 0.6^n speed loss per hit fits 150->92->44->13.
verdicts.reason: The fact is right and it is the most important consequence missing from riding. It is planned (ROADMAP.md:229 'ต่อไป: ชนแรงจนตกรถ'). But 'stays on' was a deliberate 'not too hard' choice (the test comment, and memory: user wants the game not too hard), so it must be tuned to be forgiving. It also has to come AFTER the seeing fixes (the missed sight cone, ride-02, ride-03). Throwing players off for things they could not see would feel unfair, not realistic.
verdicts.revised_observation: Nothing ends a ride except the bike breaking. Hitting 21 zombies, a wall at 150 px/s or a downed body costs speed and bike HP but never unseats you. The fall/rise poses and v.upright already exist but are unused for riders.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Add a 'thrown off' outcome to Vehicles with few, readable triggers in v1: a wall hit above CRASH (125); 3 or more zombie hits within 1 s; hitting a fat zombie above HIT_SPEED. Leave the downed-body chance for later. On a fall: dismount, slide the rider ~16-24 px along the heading with World.slide, add a new Player down state (like Zombie.down_t) drawn with the existing side-view fall, then getup_t through the existing rise, a bruise and 3-6 HP. The bike gets upright = false (draw it; see ride-04), slides ~1 cell and stalls, and E 'ยกรถ' (1 s) stands it up. Keep contact below HIT_SPEED forgiving. Replace the test at test_vehicles.gd:224 with the new rule. Ship only after the sight-cone fix and the camera zoom, so every fall has a visible cause.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. look.gd:62-67 uses thresholds 0.55 (stay side) and 0.85 (go side), so a 45-degree heading (|cos| 0.707) stays in whichever view it came from. Input is 8-way (main.gd:967-970). The ridden bike's xf = Transform2D(lean, Vector2(squash,1)...) (player.gd ~539) applies a screen-plane rotation in every view, and the squash goes down to 0.18. The headlight turns to one of 4 angles from view/dir only (player.gd ~595-598). DEPTH 0.35 (bike_art.gd:69) with front/back offsets 11*DEPTH/-10*DEPTH gives ~7 px end-on. Screenshots r1 (level side bike, dust trail going diagonal), r2 (beam straight down) and r7 (thin squashed rider) match. Caveat the lens missed: all roads are axis-aligned Rect2i (city_gen.gd:185-196), so held diagonals mostly happen on the Victory Monument circle and in turns. Every 90-degree turn still passes through the bad case, so it is frequent.
verdicts.reason: The diagnosis is right and it is the most visible artefact in motion. But the suggestion is under-costed and has a trap. Look.body_xf = xf draws the rider under the same transform, so an x-scale of |cos h| (down to ~0.55) thins the rider the same way today's mid-turn squash does, which the lens itself criticises. Getting the far/near shift right over 14 models x 3 views is visual tuning work, not S.
verdicts.revised_observation: Keyboard steering holds 0/45/90 degrees and the bike art is always drawn straight-on, so diagonals and every turn look like crabbing. The side-view lean is a screen rotation that reads as a wheelie. The headlight snaps to 4 directions. End-on, the bike is ~7 px deep beside ~3-cell-long parked cars (v05).
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Stage it. (1) One line, now: headlight.rotation from ride_seen.angle() (player.gd ~595). (2) Side view: shear the BIKE by the smoothed heading (x-axis = (|cos h|, sin h*sign(cos h)*DEPTH), y-axis = (0,1)). Draw the rider with the shear but WITHOUT the x-scale, or map seat/bar/peg anchors through the bike xf and draw the rider unscaled, so the hands stay on the bars without a thin rider. Drop the rotation lean in side view and keep it in front/back, where it reads as roll. (3) Front/back: shift the far/near parts by ±Δ along the heading. (4) Try DEPTH 0.5-0.6 in the lookbook. (5) Only then move the view switch nearer 45 degrees with hysteresis and raise the minimum squash. Check with tests/lookbook.gd.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed: CAM_LEAD 0.3 s, CAM_LEAD_MAX 48 (main.gd:107-108). The dash sits at y 542-616 of 720 (bike_dash.gd:28-31), the hotbar only fades to 0.18 (ui.gd:509), and the roof zoom-out exists (main.gd:1199). In r6 the feet are at y≈310, which fits a lead of ~45 px minus a camera lag the lens did not name: CAM_FOLLOW 12 (main.gd:111) makes cam_pos trail by ~v/12 = 12.5 px at 150 px/s, eating about a third of the lead. The '58 px' figure counts only the centre column down to the dash. The full screen shows ~100 px (0.68 s) ahead, still barely more than the ~77 px behind. The lens also missed that zombies ahead may be invisible because of the sight cone (see missed item), which is probably the bigger reason things 'appear under the wheel'.
verdicts.reason: The direction is right and cheap (zoom only, no camera angle). The numbers are slightly engineered, and the fix should include lag compensation and the sight cone.
verdicts.revised_observation: Riding N/S at zoom 4 you see ~100 px (~0.7 s) of road ahead on the full screen, and the dash covers the centre of it. The camera's soft follow lags ~12 px behind, cancelling part of the 45 px lead.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: (1) main.gd:1199: want = play_zoom * lerp(1, 0.78, roof_k) * lerp(1, 0.75, ride_k), with ride_k = ride_spd/150 smoothed over ~1 s. (2) When riding, add ride_seen / CAM_FOLLOW to the lead (cancels the lag) and raise CAM_LEAD_MAX to ~80. (3) For the rider only (not the pillion, who fights), hide the hotbar fully and move the dash to the bottom-right. (4) Measure web fps with ?perf at zoom 3 near 40 zombies. Do this together with the sight-cone fix.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. RADIUS 5 with a ±5 x ±2 foot box (vehicles.gd:15, world.gd:872-877). Slide works one axis at a time (world.gd:806-811), and a hit counts only below 50% of the step (vehicles.gd:113), so a 45-degree approach keeps ~71% and rails along the wall at full ride_vel. _park adds no blocked cell (city_gen.gd:1089-1090). Medians are ROAD tiles: my seed-11 probe found 4 median rects on 2 avenues, drawn raised in world.gd:1178-1201, and the drawing already skips junctions (in_intersection). upright is never drawn: my probe counted 58 of 515 bikes flagged fallen but drawn standing. One error in the suggestion: the 'wheel in the wall' only happens side-on (half-length 15.5 vs 5 px). End-on, the drawn wheel is ~4 px ahead against a 2 px box, so a fixed 13 px front probe would stop N/S bikes visibly short of walls.
verdicts.reason: The facts are right and the street-texture idea (kerbs, medians, scraping, parked rows) is good and Thai. The suggestion needs the probe fixed and the bundle split into cheap pieces. Drawing fallen bikes is a free realism win the lens buried.
verdicts.revised_observation: The ridden bike collides as a 10x4 px foot box. Side-on, the front wheel sinks ~10 px into walls. Angled wall contact rails at full speed with no cost. Parked bikes, kerbs and the two avenue medians do nothing. 58 bikes are flagged fallen but drawn upright.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: In order: (1) draw upright = false in StreetProp._motorbike (side art laid over, flat shadow); no gen change. (2) Front probe scaled to the drawn length: can_stand(pos + head*(13*|cos h| + 4*|sin h|), 3, road). (3) Scrape: when 50-95% of the step moves, drop the velocity's normal component, add sparks/sound, and bike HP only above BUMP. (4) Kerb crossing above ~90 px/s: ride_vel *= 0.8 plus a jolt. (5) Knock over the one parked bike you hit above HIT_SPEED (noise). Dominoes are optional. (6) Medians solid for riders only. Junction gaps are already drawn, and any mid-block U-turn gaps must use one shared rule in both world.gd:1182/1198 and collision. No GEN bump. Leave body bumps for ride-01 v2.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. mount() sets position = v.pos and plays 'door' (vehicles.gd:252-263). The 'door' sound is 'fist and shoulder against wood' (sfx.gd:248). E while riding dismounts at any speed (actions.gd:15-16). _step_off zeroes ride_vel and tries (0,9) first (vehicles.gd:309-314), which in front/back view puts you in front of or behind the wheel. The feet always use the peg anchors. moto_start is listed as wanted (audio/WANTED.md:120). r8 shows both riders stopped with feet up.
verdicts.reason: Cheap anchor/data work that makes the rider read as a person. The auto-brake before stepping off also closes the 'hop off at 60 km/h' exploit. One addition: E while grabbed is already struggle (main.gd:1529), so the auto-brake dismount must not fire while grabbed.
verdicts.revised_observation: Mounting is instant with a door-thump sound. E at any speed stops the bike dead and drops you 9 px south, which in front/back view is in front of or behind the wheel. At a standstill both riders keep their feet on the pegs.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: As proposed. (1) E above CRAWL: brake to a stop, then step off to the bike's side ((0,±9) side view, (±10,0) front/back). (2) Per-model 'start' time in vehicles.cfg (0.4 s electric start, ~1 s kick models) with a noise burst and the moto_start sound; damaged bikes may need a second try. (3) Foot down below ~8 px/s through the foot anchors, plus a small tilt in front/back. (4) A seat/stand clack instead of 'door'.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. Zombie._hold (zombie.gd:346-357) never checks distance and bites when grab_t runs out. Vehicles.server_tick (vehicles.gd:172-186) and the client prediction (main.gd:1019-1021) move the bike whatever grabbed_by says. The on-foot freeze (player.gd:297-302) is in Player.server_tick's walking path, which riders skip. The 275 px measurement could not be re-run (that part of ride_shots.gd was overwritten), but it follows from GRAB_TIME 2.2 s x speed. Extra detail: E while grabbed maps to struggle (main.gd:1529), so the grab neither holds you nor lets you hop off.
verdicts.reason: A real bug that produces an unfair long-range bite. The fix is small and creates the genre's key scene: a zombie pulling a rider off a stalled bike.
verdicts.revised_observation: A grabbed rider can ride away at full speed and is still bitten 2.2 s later from ~275 px away.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: While grabbed_by >= 0: brake to 0 in Vehicles.step (server and prediction). If the grab lands above ~30 px/s, use the ride-01 thrown-off path (falling toward the zombie). Struggle frees you as now. Release in Zombie._hold if the victim is more than ~20 px away (safety net). Add the case to test_vehicles (with grab_chance forced to 1 for that check).

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. Letting go brakes at 1.6x accel (vehicles.gd:95-99): 150->0 in 0.55 s over ~41 px. Turning never changes spd (:106-109). Radius at top speed is 150/3.2 ≈ 47 px. Noise follows speed (:204). The rider's LMB/RMB/Space do nothing (main.gd:566; req_jump returns while riding, actions.gd:138). 'บีบแตร' is planned (ROADMAP.md:197).
verdicts.reason: Throttle-based noise, grip-limited corners and a horn are good, cheap and feed the core noise system. But a 1.5 s coast at 0.5x accel, with 8-way keyboard input in 3-cell sois, makes you overshoot every turn and into the walls you now scrape (ride-04). That is a new frustration, not realism. Mouse-steer adds a second control scheme to maintain for little gain once the sight cone follows the heading.
verdicts.revised_observation: Riding has one pedal: release = hard brake, and corners are free at full speed. Engine noise tracks speed, not throttle. The rider's three combat inputs are dead while riding.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: (1) Release = engine braking ~1.0x accel (not 0.5x). Space = hard brake ~1.8x with the brake light and skid dust. (2) Grip-limited turning: max turn = GRIP/speed, and steering past it scrubs speed with dust. (3) noise = m.noise*(0.35+0.65*throttle), so rolling into your soi at night is quieter. (4) LMB = horn (~300 px lure via Main.stimulus, 1 s cooldown), which fulfils the planned 'บีบแตร'. Drop the mouse-steer option.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed: the road flag forbids FLOOR/DOOR (world.gd:889-890) and test_vehicles.gd:233-255 enforces 'a bike can't go in through a door'. The realism premise is true (Bangkok families wheel bikes into the shop front behind the shutter). But my seed-11 probe shows 515 bikes, 179 with keys and ~4.2 h of full-throttle fuel in keyed tanks, and there is no ownership yet. A bike is not worth pushing home today.
verdicts.reason: Right idea, wrong time and under-costed. It needs a new rig pose plus the bike drawn beside the walker in 4 views (near/far order). It also needs bikes in interior cells (collision, zombie pathing, doors and shutters closing on a bike, the roof fade/x-ray) and new tests. That is L, and it pays off only once bikes are scarce (missed item) and ownership exists (core rule 7, ROADMAP.md:126, and home claiming, ROADMAP.md:340-341).
verdicts.revised_observation: A bike can only be ridden or abandoned and can never enter a building. With bikes this plentiful and no ownership, pushing or storing one has no gameplay value yet.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Defer until bike scarcity and home claiming land. Then: step 1, 'เข็นรถ' on the street only (walk-holding pose via rig anchors, 0.65x walk, walking noise), useful when out of fuel. Step 2, allow parking on the ground-floor shop room of YOUR claimed home through an open shutter, and count it as yours under rule 7.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed: vehicles.cfg columns are only speed/accel/fuel/use/noise/hp/offroad/electric (data/vehicles.cfg:8-16). Turn, crawl, U-turn, brake and bump/crash are shared constants (vehicles.gd:18-31, 95, 106).
verdicts.reason: Pure data, cheap, fits 'prefer data changes', and gives the Thai street kinds a reason to differ. Impact is modest because 8-way keyboard input hides fine handling differences, so keep the column set small.
verdicts.revised_observation: Handling is identical across the 14 models apart from top speed and acceleration.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Add optional columns with defaults: turn, brake, weight (a crowd push and fall threshold for ride-01), plus start from ride-05. Example: wave/cub turn 1.2; pcx/nmax/forza turn 0.85, brake 1.2, weight 1.3; sport turn 0.75 and falls easily. Add clearance/grip only when ride-04/07 use them.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. vehicles.gd:214 subtracts damage and then :215 passes z.hp, so fx_hit (combat.gd:737-740) shows the remaining HP. fx_hit already plays 'kick' for strong hits (combat.gd:753) and vehicles.gd:216 plays another. 'stomp' maps to 'crush' (combat.gd:503-504), while 'flung' exists (corpse.gd:14, 84; rig.gd:36). The alarm only comes from bang_car (actions.gd:61-75). actions.gd:355 (the stomp action) also passes z.hp, but there it is the killing blow's full HP, so that one is correct.
verdicts.reason: Small, certain fixes to hit feedback. Low impact on their own, but they make speed read as weight.
verdicts.revised_observation: A bike hit shows the zombie's remaining HP as the damage number, plays the kick sound twice and kills with a head-crush death.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Pass speed*0.15 as dmg; drop the extra fx_sound 'kick' (or play 'crash' above ~120 px/s); _kill_zombie(..., style = 'flung') along the heading above ~100 px/s. The car alarm on a crash needs _crash to know what was hit, so keep it optional.

verdicts.fact_check: The per-bike numbers are right: fuel = m.fuel*h*0.6 (vehicles.gd:69), and a wave has 4 L at 0.012 L/s. fuelcan is uncommon in tools/store (items.cfg:781-788) and refuelling is petrol-only (vehicles.gd:332). You dismount on a zone change (main.gd:439, 445). But the root cause is missing: my seed-11 probe (CityGen.build + Vehicles.setup) found 515 bikes, 179 with keys, 918 L in tanks and ~15,100 s (4.2 h) of full-throttle riding in keyed bikes alone. Fuel doesn't matter because you just take the next bike.
verdicts.reason: Adding fuel sources first (bottle racks, coin pumps) would make fuel matter even less. The Thai fuel-source ideas are good, but only after supply is cut. The lens also didn't note that new placed props change city generation unless placed deterministically.
verdicts.revised_observation: Fuel stops mattering because keyed, fuelled bikes are everywhere (179 keyed of 515 in seed 11), not because one tank is too big.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: First cut supply (see missed item 'bike glut'). Then add Thai sources: น้ำมันขวด racks at some shop fronts, placed by hashing existing shop records (no rng draws, no GEN bump), and ตู้น้ำมันหยอดเหรียญ that need building power. Also siphoning (planned) and charging the EV from a running generator. Keep consumption as is.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. Remote riders skip NetCodec.sample_at and lerp at 15/s (player.gd:840-844). Your own bike is pulled toward net_pos at 2/s and snaps beyond 120 px (player.gd:835-839). Others arrive every other snapshot (net.gd:377, 10 Hz). INTERP 0.12 (net_codec.gd:173). turn_to for remote bikes is fed from the snapshot deltas (net.gd:428). Not measured with latency, as the lens says.
verdicts.reason: A plausible online-only problem on the fastest thing on screen. 'Measure first with 2 clients' is the right attitude. It doesn't affect host play, where the user tests.
verdicts.revised_observation: Remote bikes chase 10 Hz snapshots instead of the 120 ms interpolation walkers get, and your own predicted bike is pulled toward a round-trip-old server position.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Measure with 2 clients over a tunnel first. If it stutters: sample_at for remote riders (lean/turn from the smoothed velocity), and reconcile your own bike against the prediction from one RTT ago instead of lerping to net_pos.

verdicts.fact_check: Numbers check out: SPEED 55 (player.gd:6), KMH 0.4 (bike_dash.gd:9), and 6400 px / 55 = 116 s, /150 = 43 s, /250 = 26 s. 43 s of a 240 s day = 4.3 game hours. Bike 31 px vs parked cars ~3 cells (v05).
verdicts.reason: A useful guard-rail (don't make bikes faster or smaller), but not a finding. The clock part is already a known issue. It belongs in the direction statement, not as a ranked item.
verdicts.revised_observation: Speeds and sizes are fine. The feel problems come from seeing and contact, not the numbers.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Fold into the direction summary: keep speed, accel and human-scale bikes. Fix seeing (sight cone, camera) and contact first. The day length is tracked separately.

missed.title: Riding blind: the view cone follows the mouse, not the road
missed.observation: Sight.update sets facing = me.aim.angle() with no riding case (sight.gd:34). me.aim is the mouse minus the chest, updated every frame whatever you are doing (main.gd:972, 1009). Zombies and other players outside the 170-degree cone fade to modulate.a = sight_k -> 0 and stop being drawn (zombie.gd:738, 772; player.gd:890). The only exception is NEAR 26 px all round (sight.gd:13). The rider has no use for the mouse (can't fight, main.gd:566), so the cursor stays wherever it was. Example: riding south with the cursor above the rider, every zombie ahead is invisible until 26 px away, which is 0.17 s at 150 px/s. Meanwhile the rider's drawn head faces the road.
missed.evidence: scripts/sight.gd:27-38 (update: facing = me.aim.angle(); no riding branch); sight.gd:40-50 (sees: outside cone*0.5 or reach -> false); scripts/main.gd:972 and 1009 (aim from mouse); zombie.gd:738 (modulate.a = sight_k), zombie.gd:772 (not drawn when sight_k <= 0.01); main.gd:566 (the rider can't attack).

The pillion keeps the mouse because they fight. Add one check to test_vehicles (a zombie ahead is seen while the mouse points behind). Do this first, before ride-01.

missed.title: Bike glut: 179 ready-to-ride bikes make every bike disposable
