verdicts.direction_check: Mostly sound. It keeps speeds, sizes and the 4 views, uses systems that already exist, and uses the rule 'fast and safe on the open road, fragile and loud on contact'. That fits the scope rules and the ROADMAP (thrown off is already planned at ROADMAP.md:229, the horn at :197). Five changes: (1) The 'see' step misses its biggest cause. The sight cone follows the mouse while riding (sight.gd:34), so zombies ahead can be invisible until 26 px. Fix that and the camera-follow lag (~12 px at 150 px/s, CAM_FOLLOW 12) before anything else. (2) The 'consequences' step is undermined by supply. Seed 11 has 515 bikes, 179 of them keyed, with ~4.2 h of full-throttle fuel, so a dropped, broken or empty bike is simply swapped. Cut key/fuel supply in Vehicles.setup (data, no GEN bump) before adding falls, fuel sources or push-home, and don't add fuel sources first (ride-11). (3) Order: cheap bugs and seeing first (sight cone, headlight to heading, speed zoom, the grab bug ride-06, hit feedback ride-10, drawing fallen bikes). Then contact (front probe scaled to the drawn length, scrape, kerbs, medians). Then scarcity. Then thrown-off, tuned forgiving because the user wants a game that is 'not too hard'. Then rider actions (brake, throttle noise, horn). Push-home waits for home claiming and ownership. (4) ride-02 is right but not S: the shear must not thin the rider, and it needs lookbook tuning. (5) The lens answers only 'why motorbikes feel off'. The user also asked how to add bicycles, skateboards, cars and military vehicles realistically. Give a vehicle ladder: bicycle next (reuses BikeArt, Vehicles and anchors; quiet versus loud is a real choice), then tuk-tuk (planned; exposed rider fits the rig), then cars with a hidden driver last, army trucks as rare events. Skip skateboards.

review.summary: The motorbike stack is strong: 14 Thai-style models, 4 views, pillion, fuel, hotwiring, a headlight that zombies can see. Most of what feels off comes from two root causes. First, the 4-wheel traffic uses two projections that don't match (side-on is a flat elevation with no roof, end-on is almost straight down), and it has no heading. So every side-on car and bus faces east, every end-on car shows its headlights, tuk-tuks sit sideways on north-south roads, and rotated wrecks look like they are rearing up instead of skidded across the lane. Second, the only thing that separates vehicles is speed, in a zone you can walk across in about 2 minutes, and vehicles can't leave the zone. Direction: give each vehicle a unique trade-off in noise, seats, cargo, protection and where it fits. YES: bicycle, saleng, car/taxi. LATER, mostly as data rows or special roles: pickup, van, songthaew, tuk-tuk, army truck, long-tail boat, push cart. NO: driving the bus, skateboard, armoured vehicle. Draw every 4-wheeler with one procedural box model in the buildings' own projection (ground 1:1 with the tile grid, height straight up) at any heading, with the existing 2D details mapped onto its faces and the occupants hidden except for heads in the windows, so no new character views are needed. Build in this order: make parked cars read right and be useful (trunks, fuel) → bicycle → box renderer for parked props → saleng (it builds the car's collision, seat and cargo systems at small scale) → drivable car, and treat cars as shelters that zombies break into, not tanks.
strengths: Bikes are drawn as real Thai kinds (underbone, scooters, trail, classic) with made-up makes, in the same 4 views as characters, with far and near parts around the rider (bike_art.gd:137-190). Turn squash, lean, wheel spin, brake light and exhaust puffs (player.gd:525-561, 640-659) make riding feel physical. Keep this for all two-wheelers.

State is data-driven and deterministic: models are rows in data/vehicles.cfg, and each parked bike's fuel, key and upright state comes from its seed (vehicles.gd:57-71). Only changed vehicles are saved and synced (vehicles.gd:370-392), which matches core rule 10. Reuse exactly this for cars.

The systems already interact: engine noise feeds the stimulus system (vehicles.gd:200-204), a headlight makes you visible to zombies (zombie.gd:520), an electric bike is quiet but can't take petrol, hotwiring needs a screwdriver in hand, and a crash bruises you. These are the right kind of trade-offs to extend.
Pillion is real co-op: the passenger can fight while the rider steers (main.gd:566). It is the seed of a seats system.
The rider predicts locally with the same step() the server runs (main.gd:1017-1021), so riding feels instant online. Keep one shared step function per vehicle kind.
Parking follows Thai street life: nose to the kerb, across a soi against the wall, never across a shop front or a door (city_gen.gd:1055-1069).
Parked Thai traffic already plays a role: climbable roofs as refuges, zombies banging on cars and setting off alarms (actions.gd:61-89, zombie.gd:284-291), cream/red buses and red/blue songthaews.
MeshCanvas turns a static drawing into one triangle batch and supports any affine transform (mesh_canvas.gd:33-53). That makes a code-drawn box model cheap.
Rotated end-on wrecks already read convincingly as skidded cars (v05 top, v12 centre). A shape seen mostly from above rotates well, which supports the box-model direction.

findings.title: Differentiate vehicles by noise, seats, cargo, protection and where they fit, not by speed
findings.observation: Fact: the 14 rideable models differ only in speed (145-250 px/s), tank size (3.7-15 L), noise (60-420 px), hp and an offroad flag. All carry 2 people and no cargo. Walking the full 400-cell zone width takes about 116 s (6400 px / 55 px/s), and from spawn to an edge about 60 s. A big scooter does the full width in about 35 s. Vehicles can't leave the zone: travel() dismounts everyone. The ~300 parked 4-wheelers are scenery and roof refuges only.
findings.evidence: data/vehicles.cfg:18-157; player.gd:6 (SPEED 55); data/zones/victory.cfg size=[400,320]; main.gd:439 and 444-445 (vehicles.dismount on travel); street_prop.gd:12 (CLIMB). References: 7 Days to Die separates bicycle (no fuel), minibike, motorcycle and 4x4 by storage (27/36/81 slots) and seats (4x4 carries the group); Project Zomboid gates cars on keys, hotwiring and siphoning; State of Decay 2 zombies rip doors off and drag occupants out.
findings.why: Every vehicle is much faster than walking, so a new one that is only a bit faster or slower feels like a reskin. The core loop needs decisions: quiet or fast, carry loot or carry friends, safe inside or able to fight, fits the soi or not. It is also how Bangkok actually works: each vehicle exists for what it carries and where it fits (saleng for cargo, songthaew for people, motorbikes through jams).
findings.suggestion:
Adopt this role matrix (seats = driver + N):
- Bicycle: YES, 1st. About 100-110 px/s, just above a sprint but sustained. Near-silent (about 30). 1 + 1 side-saddle on the rack. Basket of 2-3 slots. Wheel it through doors. Costs stamina and thirst, no fuel. The only truly quiet vehicle.
- Saleng (motorbike with a left-side cargo tray): YES, 2nd. About 120 px/s, bike noise. 1 + 2 in the tray, who can fight. Tray of 12-16 slots plus bulky things (gas bottle, water jar, generator). 1.6 cells wide, so no wreck gaps. Petrol. Role: hauling home.
- Car/taxi: YES, 3rd. About 160 px/s. Medium engine, but loud doors, crashes and horn. 1 + 3, trunk of about 12. Protects you until the glass breaks. Roads and single-lane sois, stopped by jams. Petrol 35-45 L; taxis run on LPG/NGV. Role: a shelter on wheels.
- Pickup: LATER, as a car data row. 2 in the cab + 4 in the bed who can fight. Role: a moving fighting platform for a co-op group.
- Van: LATER, car variant, 1 + 9 enclosed. Fits Victory Monument's old van terminal. Ambulance = van variant with medical loot and a siren lure.
- Songthaew: LATER, pickup variant with 8-10 bench seats and a roof you can stand on. Otherwise NO.
- Tuk-tuk: LATER (already in ROADMAP phase 5), only with its own trade-off: runs on LPG from the kitchen gas bottles (cook or drive), narrow enough for wreck gaps, tips over in fast turns, open cab so the driver can be grabbed. Without that it duplicates the saleng.
- Army truck: LATER, as a group objective (key on the dead officer at the checkpoint, diesel, battery). 2 + 12, huge cargo, very loud, climbs kerbs and grass.
- Long-tail boat: LATER. Canal only, loud, 1 + 4, zombies can't follow (reuse the swim rules).
- Push cart/trolley: LATER, folded into 'drag furniture'. Walking pace, rattles, the only haul that goes through doors.
- NO: driving the bus (147 px long, can't turn into a 48 px soi, its role is covered by van and songthaew; keep it as a parked refuge and loot spot), skateboard (duplicates the bicycle and is useless on broken pavement), armoured vehicle (invulnerable = not scary; duplicates the truck), pedal saleng/samlor and kick scooter (duplicate the bicycle and the EV bike).
Also let vehicles cross zone exits with you. That gives distance a purpose now that zones stay small.
findings.scope_check: Design only. Every YES either reuses the 4-view bike/rider rig (bicycle, saleng) or is a rigid body drawn with the box model, which needs no character views. The roles are data columns in vehicles.cfg: seats, slots, noise, fuel type, width. Nothing redraws every frame beyond what bikes already do.

findings.title: Staged plan: parked cars right and useful → bicycle → box renderer on parked props → saleng → drivable car
findings.observation: The car is the most-wanted vehicle but the biggest system. It needs rendering at any heading, a non-circle collision, a new steering model, seats, doors, a trunk, zombies attacking the car, a heading on the wire and save changes. None of these exist yet. The bike stack exists and can absorb a bicycle almost for free.
findings.evidence: vehicles.gd (bike-only: RADIUS 5, rider/pillion, view/dir); street_prop.gd:235-357 (parked 4-wheelers are 2 hand-drawn views); ROADMAP phase 2 'ค้นท้ายรถ บีบแตร ดูดน้ำมัน', phase 5 'ตุ๊กตุ๊ก เรือหางยาว'.
findings.why: Rule: one system at a time, each step playable. The smallest step that adds the most play is the one that changes a decision on every trip (quiet bicycle; fuel and loot from cars) without new tech. De-risk the car by shipping its renderer on parked props first (no gameplay risk) and its collision, seats and cargo on the saleng (small scale).
findings.suggestion:
Stage 0 (S, about a week, no GEN bump): fix parked-traffic direction and scales (V06). Make parked vehicles useful: search trunks and delivery boxes, siphon fuel with a hose (V05). Camera look-ahead and headlight fixes (V13).
Stage 1 (S-M): bicycle (V09), plus pushing a bike through a door and keeping the key in your pocket (V08).
Stage 2 (M, 1-2 weeks): VehicleArt box renderer (V03), used only for parked cars, taxis, vans, pickups, songthaews, buses, tuk-tuks, army trucks and wrecks. Measure on web with F3 and ?bench.
Stage 3 (M, 1-2 weeks): saleng (V10). It brings multi-disc collision, non-leaning steering with a turning radius, a vehicle container and 3 seats.
Stage 4 (L, 3-5 weeks): drivable car/taxi (V11, V12, V04, V14). After that, pickup, van, songthaew and ambulance are data rows (S each).
Stage 5 (LATER): tuk-tuk on LPG, army truck as a group objective, long-tail boat, vehicles crossing zones.
findings.scope_check: Each stage is either data, a system, or one reusable renderer. No stage adds a character view. Generation changes are appended last with their own seed (the city_gen.gd:1183-1186 pattern), so no GEN bump until jams (V07).

findings.title: Draw every 4-wheeler with one procedural box model in the buildings' projection, not with fixed views
findings.observation: Today's cars mix two projections. Side-on is a flat elevation: body plus cabin with only a 1.2-unit roof strip, full height about 27 px (street_prop.gd:241-248). End-on is almost straight down: 26 units of roof/bonnet over a 5-unit face (street_prop.gd:266-270). Neither matches the buildings, where the facade rises straight up by h and the roof is the footprint at 1:1 lifted by h (building_prop.gd:154-156, 164). The tuk-tuk and the army truck got only one view each, which shows what hand-drawn views cost. Rotating a side elevation makes the car pitch nose-up instead of skidding across the lane. The rotated end view reads fine.
findings.evidence: street_prop.gd:147-157, 235-276, 372-384, 681-695; building_prop.gd:3-5, 154-164; v17_bus_z4 right edge (x≈1040-1270, y≈160-300): black side-on wreck rotated → reads as rearing up; v05_night_ride_z3 top and v12_taxi_z4 centre: rotated end-on wrecks read as skidded. v14/v15/v16: end-on van, pickup and songthaew read as plain coloured slabs. mesh_canvas.gd:33-53 (any Transform2D applies to every draw call).
findings.why: Driven cars spend most of their time at diagonal headings. (a) 4 fixed views with snapping makes a 3-cell rigid body crab sideways at 45°. On a bike or a person the rider hides that; on a car it is the single most 'off' thing a player will see. 8 views doubles the art and every new kind needs all of them. (b) A box model is correct at every heading. It is consistent with the buildings, with the tile grid (the footprint you see is the footprint that collides) and with parked props (same renderer). A new kind is a data row. (c) A flat top-down sprite rotated freely (GTA2 style) rotates well but reads as a decal in a 3/4 world with upright people and facades, and loses roof height, which roof climbing needs. Real 3D through a SubViewport clashes with PointLight2D night lighting, y-sort and the web budget.
findings.suggestion:
Pick (b). New file scripts/vehicle_art.gd, about 200 lines:
1. Each part (body, cabin, bed, canopy) is a box in local coordinates: x along, y across, z up, with an optional inset at the top front and back for sloped screens.
2. Rotate x,y by the heading and project with the buildings' rule: screen = (wx, wy - z). Ground stays 1:1 with the tile grid. Heights use the character scale (a car roof about 27 px, like today), so people standing on roofs still line up.
3. Draw the top face always. Draw a vertical face only if its rotated outward normal has +y (it faces the camera). Order parts bottom to top and far to near.
4. Shade like the buildings: top lighter, faces darker toward the bottom.
5. Wheels are dark ellipses on the visible side faces.
6. Every detail (windows, lights, taxi sign, bus windows, songthaew rails) is a 'decal' drawn in face-local (u, v) through c.draw_set_transform_matrix(face affine). Today's _car_side, _car_end and _thai_* code becomes these decals, so the current art is kept.
Data rows in vehicles.cfg, for example:
[sedan]
name="คาเซะ ซิตี้"
class="car"
size=[52,22]
parts=[["body",-26,26,-11,11,3,13,0,0],["cabin",-12,12,-10,10,13,26,5,3]]
wheels=[[-16,4.5],[16,4.5]]
seats=[[-2,-5],[-2,5],[-14,-5],[-14,5]]
trunk=12
decals=["sedan_side","sedan_front","sedan_back"]
speed=160.0
turn_radius=60.0
reverse=55.0
fuel=40.0
fuel_type="petrol"
noise=240.0
hp=200
glass=30
Redraw only when the heading byte (256 steps, as NetCodec.angle_byte) or state changes: window broken, door open, lights. Moving only moves the node. Y-sort by the footprint centre. Split the bus and army truck into two sort nodes only if errors show. roof_spot, roof_area, middle, draw_shift, VEHICLE_SCALE, BODY and _read_boxes (street_prop.gd:10-99, world.gd:830-866) become values computed from the data.
findings.scope_check: (1) No character views: people in closed vehicles are heads behind glass (Look._head, already called from outside Look at top_rig.gd:125), and people on open seats use the existing ride and sit poses. (2) One renderer; each new vehicle is a data row plus optional decals. (3) Parked cars are drawn once (MeshCanvas, streamed). A moving car rebuilds about 150-250 triangles only when its heading byte changes, far below one animated character. Measure with perf_overlay after stage 2.

findings.title: Make a car a shelter that zombies break into, not a tank
findings.observation: Fact: zombies can lunge at, bite and grab a rider (zombie.gd:189-195). Ground bites skip riders (zombie.gd:174, 296). Against a target on a car roof they bang and may start the alarm (zombie.gd:284-291, actions.gd:61-89, 25% once). A moving bike above 60 px/s knocks zombies flat and loses 3 hp per zombie (vehicles.gd:206-226). There is no idea yet of a closed vehicle with windows, doors or people inside.
findings.evidence: zombie.gd:174, 189-195, 284-296, 335-342 (grab/struggle); vehicles.gd:18, 206-226, 230-243; actions.gd:61-89; State of Decay 2: clinging zombies damage the car, rip doors off and drag survivors out; Project Zomboid: broken windows are a way in.
findings.why: If a car is safe, it deletes the danger → decide steps of the loop. If it is a death trap, nobody drives. The fear that works, and that players will film, is sitting in a car while the horde surrounds it and a window cracks. It stays simple: the zombies bang on the car's sides with their existing attack, no new poses.
findings.suggestion:
Server-side vehicle state: glass hp per side (4), doors, hp.
- A stopped or slow car: zombies within reach of a side bang it (reuse bang_car timing, the noise and the alarm chance on a first hotwire failure).
- A side with 0 glass lets a lunging zombie grab the occupant of the nearest seat on that side (reuse grab, struggle and bite_part). A failed struggle pulls them out: dismount to that side.
- Each zombie in contact with the front cuts speed by about 15%, so a horde can stop a car. At speed, reuse the knock-down code with the car's front edge as the probe, costing car hp and cracking the windscreen.
- Horn (ROADMAP 'บีบแตร'): a 500 px noise lure. Leave a car honking as a decoy.
- Doors: getting in or out takes about 0.8 s and makes a noise of about 120.
- Occupants of closed seats can't attack; people on open seats (pickup bed, saleng tray, pillion) can.
- Hiding in a parked car at night: zombies ignore you unless they saw you get in or you make noise.
findings.scope_check: No new zombie art: they use the existing attack and bang pose at the car's side cells. Occupants are hidden (V12), so no new character views. Pure systems, reusing stimulus, grab and alarm. Cost per tick is O(zombies near the car), the same as the bike hit loop.

findings.title: Make the parked vehicles useful now: trunks, delivery boxes, fuel siphoning
findings.observation: About 300 parked 4-wheelers line every avenue, but you can only climb them. Delivery boxes are drawn on about 20% of wave/click/pcx bikes (bike_art.gd:98-100, 193-198) but are paint only. Fuel only comes from jerrycans (vehicles.gd:329-340). Electric bikes can never be recharged: refuel returns early for them (vehicles.gd:332). Containers only exist as furniture nodes: inventory refs ['box', cid, idx] index world.container_nodes (inventory.gd:22-26, 93-99; FurnitureProp.SIZE 8 at furniture_prop.gd:6).
findings.evidence: street_prop.gd:12 (CLIMB list), interact.gd:106, 219 (only 'climb' for street cars); bike_art.gd:193-198; vehicles.gd:329-340; inventory.gd:22-26, 39-75; ROADMAP phase 2 'ค้นท้ายรถ บีบแตร ดูดน้ำมัน'; PZ: siphoning needs an empty can and a hose.
findings.why: This feeds the core loop right away. Avenues full of cars become a place worth the risk: fuel, luggage, a first-aid kit in the glovebox, a food order gone off in a rider's box. It also builds the container and vehicle-state generalization the drivable car needs, before any movement code.
findings.suggestion:
1. Generalize container refs to container records: add ['veh', id, idx], or give each vehicle a container dict with its own size, not tied to FurnitureProp.
2. Loot tables by kind: sedan/taxi trunk (luggage, umbrella, water, jack as a weapon), pickup bed (tools, sacks), van (evacuee bags), ambulance (medical), songthaew/bus (bags, school uniforms), delivery box on a bike (food orders that spoil via Items spoil), army truck (MRE, sandbags, radio).
3. Siphon: needs a hose (new recipe from scrap or garden hose) and an empty fuel can. 6 s. Makes noise. Car tanks 5-30 L by seed. Taxis hold LPG, which a hose can't take.
4. Popping a locked trunk with a crowbar: noisy, alarm chance.
5. Electric bikes recharge at any building with power (Buildings power, generator): quiet, but ties you to a lit building.
findings.scope_check: Data plus system: loot rows in items.cfg tables and one container abstraction. No new art beyond an open trunk lid, which is a decal. Seed-derived state and a saved diff, like bikes. No GEN bump: the props already exist, and their state comes from the seed without drawing random numbers.

findings.title: Parked traffic reads wrong: backwards lanes, a toy-sized army truck, a tuk-tuk that looks like a food cart
findings.observation: 1) Every side-on car, van and bus faces east (headlight at the right end, tail at the left), and every end-on one shows its headlights (faces south), whatever lane it is in. Thailand drives on the left, so about half of them are parked backwards. The lane is chosen from [0,1,wd-2,wd-1] and no direction is stored. 2) Tuk-tuks are always side-on (`horizontal or kind == "tuktuk"`), so on north-south roads they sit across the lane. They are 16 units (1.6 cells) long, with no cab, front wheel or handlebars, and read like the noodle cart. 3) The army truck's canvas top is at -12 units (≈19 px) against a car cabin at -17 (≈27 px) and a person at ≈30 px, so it is lower than a sedan. It has one view. 4) Flipped end-on wrecks draw a 26-unit underside bar on a 16-unit-wide car, so a dark bar sticks out sideways. The `Color("2a2622") if side else Color("2a2622")` shows a side/end difference was intended but not done.
findings.evidence: street_prop.gd:257-258, 270-272, 326-327, 353-355 (fixed light positions); city_gen.gd:921-923, 986; street_prop.gd:372-384 vs 392-407 (_cart); 684-693 and 26 (army height, roof_spot 12*k); 458-459 (flip bar). Screenshots: v17_bus_z4 (bus and car in the north lanes facing east); v01_ride_side_z4 (blue car top, north lanes, facing east); v13_tuktuk_z4 (tuk-tuk at x≈530-635 across Phahon Yothin, beside the similar-looking cart); v18_army_z4 (truck top y≈190, ground ≈270 → ≈20 px; player ≈29 px); 12_ratchawithi (white wreck, bar ≈x990-1110, y180-220); v12_taxi_z4 (bar ≈x770-920).
findings.why: Traffic direction is one of the first things a Thai player reads subconsciously. A street where every car points the same way reads as a toy set. A military truck shorter than a sedan breaks the scale the characters set. These props are on screen every trip.
findings.suggestion:
Cheap fixes now (S, no GEN bump: nothing draws random numbers):
(a) Direction at draw time from the lane: on a horizontal road, cells north of the centre face west and cells south face east. On a vertical road, the west half faces south (front to camera) and the east half faces north (draw the rear: red tail lights, no headlights). Mirror the side view with scale.x = -1 about its middle. Better still, lay down a jam direction per road (V07).
(b) Army truck: canvas top ≈ -28 units, cab ≈ -22; update roof_spot.
(c) Tuk-tuk: draw it the right way along vertical roads (end view) and give it the curved cab roof, a single front wheel and a bench at 20-22 units long; later it becomes a box-model row.
(d) Flip bar width: 26 if side else 12. The flipped end view should show the underside (dark chassis, 4 wheels), not a mirrored roof.
All of this is superseded by V03, but it is worth doing now because it is visible everywhere.
findings.scope_check: Art tweaks inside existing views and props, redrawn once (streamed, MeshCanvas). No generation RNG change, so no GEN bump.

findings.title: The city must be hard to drive, or vehicles have no trade-offs: jams, gaps and parked bikes
findings.observation: Generation deliberately never blocks a lane: 'Keep a gap so vehicles never wall off a lane completely'. Traffic is sparse (length/7 attempts per road, random lanes). Wrecks are length/22 per road plus pile-ups at 65% of junctions. The wide avenues read empty and open. Parked motorbikes are not solid to other vehicles: slide() only checks tiles and blocked cells, and bikes are not in w.blocked.
findings.evidence: city_gen.gd:917-923, 973-976, 995-1019; 12_ratchawithi and 16_wide (open carriageways); vehicles.gd:112 and world.gd:780-812 (slide against tiles and blocked); vehicles.gd:70 (upright flag exists).
findings.why: If every avenue is clear, a car is simply better than a bike, a bicycle or walking, and the 'access' column of the role matrix means nothing. A real outbreak in Bangkok means gridlock on the outbound roads (Phahon Yothin north toward Don Mueang, Ratchawithi), abandoned mid-lane, doors open. That is realistic, tells the story, and forces the choice: bike through the gaps, car round by the sois, or on foot.
findings.suggestion:
With the car stage (it needs a GEN bump anyway), or appended last from its own seed:
- Add `jams=[{rect, dir}]` to the zone file (data): dense same-direction lines of cars (doors open, some burnt) on outbound carriageways, with 1-cell gaps a bike or bicycle can thread and a car can't. Put the direction in each record (fixes V06a for free).
- Keep side streets and the opposite carriageway drivable.
- A moving car hitting a parked motorbike knocks it over (upright=false, a clatter of about 200 noise): reuses the existing flag.
- Co-op: 2+ players can push a parked car in neutral about 1 cell a second to open a lane. It is saved as a moved vehicle. This is not destruction: the city stays, you rearrange a car.
findings.scope_check: Zone data plus the existing _vehicle and _wreck placement (it respects the user's GEN-bump preference if appended last with its own seed). No new art: the same parked props with a stored direction. Pushing reuses the moved-vehicle state from V14.

findings.title: Vehicles and home: wheel the bike inside at night, keep the key in your pocket
findings.observation: Bikes treat FLOOR and DOOR tiles as walls (`road` flag), so you can never bring your bike home. Once any player hotwires a bike, `v.key = true` for everyone, so on a 20-50 player server anyone can ride off on 'your' bike. Parked bikes are only ever at kerbs and soi walls.
findings.evidence: vehicles.gd:112 (slide(..., road=true)); world.gd:780, 821, 889 (road → FLOOR/DOOR solid); vehicles.gd:321-326, 351-361 (key is a global bool); ROADMAP core rule 7 'เจ้าของและสิทธิ์ ... รถ (คนเดียว/กลุ่ม)'; ROADMAP 'จับจองบ้าน' (home claiming).
findings.why: Realism: every Thai shophouse family wheels its motorbikes into the ground-floor shop at night and pulls down the rolling shutter. It is one of the most recognizable daily rituals, and it ties the vehicle to the home loop (go home, secure things). Online, a vehicle you can't keep is a vehicle nobody invests in (fuel, repairs, cargo). This matches the existing rule: bikes are still never parked across a shop front or in a doorway; they go fully inside.
findings.suggestion: 1) 'Push' mode (dismount while holding E, or an action 'จูงรถ'): you walk at 0.7× beside the bike, engine off, using the existing walking rig with hands on the bars (anchors), and you can pass 1-cell doors and roll-up shutters. Parking indoors is just a vehicle position on FLOOR, saved like any moved bike. 2) Keys as items: riding away with a found key puts 'กุญแจ <model>' in your inventory. Hotwiring gives no key, but you can lock the steering. Without the key, others must hotwire (8 s, needs a screwdriver, makes noise, alarm chance). Group members share keys by handing them over. 3) Later, with home claiming: a vehicle parked inside your claimed home counts as yours.
findings.scope_check: Uses the existing 4 views and rig anchors (a walking pose with hands on the bars is the same kind of thing as the pillion anchors). Keys are rows in items.cfg. Only one new rule in slide: in push mode, don't pass the road flag. No per-frame cost.

findings.title: Bicycle first: the one quiet vehicle, almost free to build
findings.observation: All rideable vehicles make engine noise (180-420) except the EV scooter (60), and the EV's battery can never be refilled. Nothing between a sprint (≈96 px/s, drains stamina) and a motorbike (150+ px/s, loud, needs fuel) lets you travel quietly with no fuel.
findings.evidence: data/vehicles.cfg (noise column; ev 98-107); vehicles.gd:332 (electric can't refuel); survival.gd:196-200 (sprint stamina, footstep noise); bike_art.gd:39-54, 105-128 (rider/pillion anchors per model); 7 Days to Die: bicycle is the no-fuel starter vehicle.
findings.why: It adds the most play for the smallest step: every trip gets a new choice (quiet and steady, or loud and fast). It gives new players a first vehicle that doesn't need a screwdriver, and it is peak Bangkok realism: mother's bikes with a front basket, kids' BMX, people riding side-saddle on the rear rack.
findings.suggestion:
Add 3 rows to vehicles.cfg with a `pedal=true` flag: city bike with a basket, BMX, and a made-up bike-share bike. Speed 100-110, accel 110, noise 25-35 (a chain rattle), hp 30, no fuel and no key. Stamina drains at about 40% of sprinting, a little thirst. Stamina at 0 means coasting only. A bell is a 120 px lure.
Draw them with new BikeArt model functions in the same far/near structure: a frame triangle, thin wheels, a basket. The pedalling pose is the feet anchors moving round a crank circle driven by wheel_turn, so clothes follow via the rig.
Pillion sits side-saddle on the rack (a pillion_anchors variant).
Place them by appending last with their own seed: at shophouse fronts, the BTS station, the market, hospital staff areas. That keeps existing vehicle ids and saves stable.
The basket is a 3-slot container (V05). Bicycles can be pushed indoors (V08).
findings.scope_check: Uses the existing 4 views and far/near rider layering. The new pose (pedalling) goes through Rig anchors, as the rules require. Mostly data rows plus a few BikeArt draw functions. Per frame it costs the same as a ridden bike (one rider).

findings.title: Saleng (motorbike with a sidecar tray): the Thai cargo vehicle, and the bridge to cars
findings.observation: No vehicle carries cargo or more than 2 people. Bike collision is a flat 10×4 px footprint (RADIUS 5 with FOOT_DEPTH 0.4), and steering can pivot on the spot below CRAWL. Neither can represent a 3-wheeler that is 1.6 cells wide and can't lean.
findings.evidence: vehicles.gd:15, 97-99; world.gd:872-877 (_feet: r × 0.4r); bike_art.gd:137-190 (4-view bike drawing that a tray can attach to); ROADMAP 'ระบบน้อยแต่ชนกันเยอะ' (few systems, many interactions).
findings.why: Salengs are everywhere in Bangkok (scrap collectors, ice and vegetable vendors), so it is authentic and fills the 'haul it home' role the core loop lacks (water jars, gas bottles, a generator, a sack of rice). Technically it is the car's systems at small scale on top of a known rider: multi-disc collision, a turning radius without pivoting, a container on a vehicle, 3 seats, and the box renderer used at the 4 snapped headings. The car becomes much less risky afterwards.
findings.suggestion:
A vehicles.cfg row with class="saleng", base="wave" (the rider bike art), a tray box of [26×14 px, z 3-10] on the left side (the kerb side in Thailand), seats [driver, tray×2], tray of 14 slots, and `bulky=true` (accepts gas bottle, water jar, generator).
Draw the bike with BikeArt at its snapped view and the tray with VehicleArt at the same snapped heading. Facing east the tray is on the far side, drawn behind; facing west it is on the near side, drawn in front. Tray passengers use the existing sit pose and can fight (like pillion).
Collision is 2-3 discs (V11). No lean, turn radius about 40 px, tips over if turning hard above 80% speed with an empty tray. Noise as a wave. Petrol.
Replace some kerb bikes near the market and the ร้านวัสดุ (hardware) and ขายส่ง (wholesale) shops by appending last with their own seed.
findings.scope_check: The rider and bike use the existing 4 views. The tray is a rigid box from the box renderer at 4 headings, so no character view is needed. Passengers use the existing sit pose. Data row plus systems that the car reuses. It costs one rider plus up to 2 sitting characters per frame, like a bike with pillion.

findings.title: Movement model per kind: multi-disc collision, real turning radius, reverse, heading as its own state on the wire
findings.observation: 1) Collision: every vehicle is the rider's 10×4 px foot, while a side-on bike is drawn about 34 px long, so the front wheel enters walls before a hit registers. 2) Steering is absolute WASD. Below CRAWL a bike 'points anywhere' (pivots on the spot). Steering more than 2.3 rad back only brakes. There is no reverse. 3) There is no heading: a vehicle stores view/dir strings picked from velocity. Other clients work out a rider's heading from snapshot deltas. Riders are not interpolated from samples like walkers (they use lerp 15·delta). Local prediction snaps back if more than 120 px off.
findings.evidence: vehicles.gd:15, 21-27, 83-119 (step), 97-99, 103-104, 147-155; city_gen.gd:1091-1093 (a bike covers ±17 px); world.gd:780-827, 872-877; net.gd:425-431; player.gd:836-844; NetCodec.angle_byte at net_codec.gd:21-26 (unused for vehicles).
findings.why: The most 'off' possible car moment is one that pivots in place or slides sideways. A car also has to reverse out of a dead-end soi. A heading worked out from motion flips 180° the moment a car reverses, so every other player would see it drive backwards facing the wrong way.
findings.suggestion:
Per class in data: `turn_radius`, `wheelbase`, `reverse`, `grip`, `can_pivot` (true only for 2-wheelers).
- 4-wheelers use a kinematic bicycle model: yaw rate = speed / wheelbase · tan(steer). Steer eases toward the angle to the WASD direction, clamped to about 35°. The radius grows with speed² above a grip limit. No turning at zero speed. Keep absolute WASD so walking, bikes and cars share one control scheme: aiming more than 120° behind the heading while slower than CRAWL engages reverse (about 55 px/s). Space = handbrake. Offer relative 'tank' controls as an option only if playtests ask for it.
- Collision: 3 discs along the axis (radius W/2), each checked with a square footprint, not the FOOT_DEPTH-flattened one, against tiles, blocked cells and the road flag. Rotation is blocked if a disc would enter a wall (scrape). Hits against characters use the rotated rectangle plus a margin, generalizing vehicles.gd:209.
- State: v.heading (float) and v.gear. Snapshots add a u8 heading (angle_byte) and a flags byte (reverse, brake, lights, horn), about 2 bytes per driver. Clients interpolate driven vehicles with NetCodec.sample_at plus lerp_angle. Correct the driver's prediction if heading error is above about 20°.
- Passengers stay slaved to the driver, as pillion is today (player.gd:814-819).
findings.scope_check: Pure systems; no art. Per tick it is a few can_stand calls per driven vehicle. Bandwidth is +2 bytes per driving player against a 15 KB/s budget.

findings.title: Seats, doors and occupants: hide bodies in closed vehicles, show heads in the windows
findings.observation: Seating is two fixed roles: v.rider/v.pillion and Player.seat 0/1. Dismount tries 4 fixed offsets. The rider and pillion are drawn fully as characters by the rider's node, which interleaves bike parts and bodies.
findings.evidence: vehicles.gd:70, 252-314; player.gd:141-143, 525-581; main.gd:566 (pillion can fight); top_rig.gd:125 (Look._head is callable on its own).
findings.why: Co-op needs 4-12 seats (car, van, pickup bed, songthaew). Drawing full bodies inside a car would need them clipped by the doors, cost a full character per occupant per frame, and look wrong at diagonal headings. Real cars mostly hide their occupants anyway.
findings.suggestion:
- v.seats: Array of peer ids (seat 0 drives), with per-model seat anchors (local x,y,z) and `open` flags in data.
- E near a vehicle picks the nearest free seat by door position (anchor rotated by heading). Getting in or out takes about 0.8 s with a door-open decal. Exit goes to that door's side (first free of door side, rear, other side).
- Closed seats: the occupant's Player node skips drawing. VehicleArt draws each occupied closed seat as Look._head in FRONT/BACK/SIDE (picked with Look.pick_view from the heading) behind the glass decal (dark, alpha about 0.55), so heads read as silhouettes. It redraws when occupants change.
- Open seats (pickup bed, saleng tray, tuk-tuk bench, songthaew benches) use the existing sit/ride poses at their anchors, snapped to the nearest of the 4 views. At diagonals the body is turned while the vehicle isn't, which reads as fine because people sit at angles.
- Standing on the roof of a moving pickup, songthaew or bus: on_car players move with the vehicle.
findings.scope_check: No new views: heads use existing Look._head views, bodies use existing sit and ride poses. A car of 4 friends draws 4 heads instead of 4 full animated characters, which is cheaper than walking. The data rows hold the seats.

findings.title: At speed you can't see what's coming, and the headlight points 45° off at diagonals
findings.observation: The camera leads a rider by 0.3 s, capped at 48 px. At the default zoom 4 on 1280×720 the view is 320×180 world px. Riding north or south (every soi) you see about 90 + 48 = 138 px ahead: 0.92 s at 150 px/s, 0.76 s at 182, 0.55 s on the sport bike (250). East or west it is about 208 px (1.4 / 1.1 / 0.83 s). The headlight turns only to the 4 snapped views, so riding diagonally the beam points up to 45° away from where you are going.
findings.evidence: main.gd:107-108, 1028-1037; player.gd:594-599; look.gd:62-67 (side view kept until |cos| < 0.55); v02_ride_soi_front_z4 and v03_ride_soi_back_z4 (little soi visible ahead); v05_night_ride_z3 (beam straight up while riding).
findings.why: At under a second of warning, zombies and wrecks appear already under your wheel. Crashes then feel unfair rather than like a bad decision. Cars (longer, faster, can't dodge) make it worse. The night beam is also a stimulus zombies see, so it should point where the bike actually goes.
findings.suggestion: 1) Zoom out with speed: target zoom lerps from the player's zoom to about 0.75× of it at full speed and back when slowing (the zoom range 1-6 already exists). 2) Allow a longer lead along y than x (for example cap 48 horizontal / 80 vertical) to make up for the 16:9 aspect. 3) Headlight rotation = the angle of ride_seen (or ride_vel for the local rider), not the view. 4) For cars, the brake and reverse lights come from the flags byte (V11).
findings.scope_check: Only camera zoom and a light's rotation; not a new camera angle or rotation. No art. No per-frame cost.

findings.title: Vehicle ids, saves and world caches aren't ready for more vehicle kinds
findings.observation: Vehicles.setup gives each bike id = its index while walking street_props in order. Cars are placed in the same loops as kerb bikes (_street_furniture), so they are interleaved in street_props. Saves store changed vehicles by that id. Parked cars are baked into w.blocked, AStar, the `_low` cache and the `_boxes` cache, and the caches are built once and never invalidated.
findings.evidence: vehicles.gd:60-71, 370-392; city_gen.gd:917-946, 1044-1069 (cars and bikes interleaved); save_game.gd:123, 179; world.gd:615-642 (_props_read), 832-866 (_boxes_read), 233 (street_props[i].id).
findings.why: If cars join the same setup pass, every existing bike id shifts and old saves restore fuel, damage and position onto the wrong bikes. When a parked car first moves, its old cells must stop being walls for zombies and players, and a car parked at an angle must become an obstacle for pathfinding. Without that, zombies walk through parked cars or around invisible ones.
findings.suggestion:
- Key vehicles by street_prop id (rec.id, already assigned in world.gd:233) or by a per-kind id space, and keep the old bike index mapping for existing saves.
- Add World.unblock_vehicle(rec) and block_footprint(v): erase or add cells in blocked, set AStar points solid, clear the _low and _boxes entries. Rasterize a stopped moved car's rotated footprint to the cells it covers by at least 50%, skipping cells with someone standing in them; is_low for the bonnet cells.
- Save per vehicle: pos, heading, fuel, hp, glass[4], doors, trunk items, key owner, moved flag.
- Stream parked cars as now; switch one to owned (always in the scene) once touched, like bikes.
- Make the vehicle record self-contained (model, seed, colour, state, items) so it can later travel across zone exits.
findings.scope_check: Data and system plumbing only; no art. Changing cells happens only on park and unpark events, not per frame. No GEN bump: ids come from existing records.

verdicts.fact_check: Mostly correct. data/vehicles.cfg:18-157: 14 models differ in speed 145-250, accel, fuel 3.7-15, use, noise 60-420, hp 45-80, offroad, electric. None has seats or cargo fields. Pillion is the only second seat (vehicles.gd:267-280). Zone is size=[400,320] (data/zones/victory.cfg). 6400/55 = 116 s. main.gd:439 and 444-445 dismount everyone on travel. One nuance the lens missed: the dash scale (bike_dash.gd:9, KMH 0.4) makes a Wave about 60 km/h but walking (55 px/s) about 22 km/h. So in the game a bike is only about 2.7x walking, where in real life it is about 10x. Speed really cannot be the thing that separates vehicles, which supports the lens's point.
verdicts.reason: The principle is right and it is the actual answer to the user's 'which direction' question: vehicles differ by role (noise, seats, cargo, protection, where they fit). But the 12-row matrix is too much for a solo beginner to hold, and it mixes near-term work with far-future rows. 'Vehicles cross zone exits' depends on server-to-server travel that the ROADMAP marks as not yet tried with several programs ('ยังไม่ได้ลองกับหลายโปรแกรมจริง', line 309), so it is not a near-term suggestion. Skateboard as a flat NO is defensible for realism. The ROADMAP does accept joke items (A3 ของปั่น), though, so it could come back later as a rare novelty, never as a vehicle class.
verdicts.revised_observation: Rideable bikes differ only in speed, fuel, noise, hp and offroad. None has cargo or more than one passenger. Because the zone is small and the game squeezes vehicle speed to about 2.7x walking (real life: about 10x), speed alone cannot make a new vehicle feel different.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Adopt the principle 'each vehicle = a different trade-off' and add the columns to vehicles.cfg as vehicles need them: seats, slots, noise, fuel_type, width, pedal. Commit to only two new kinds now: bicycle (quiet, no fuel, costs stamina) and later saleng (hauling). Keep the car as a decision gate after those (see V02/V03). Park pickup, van, songthaew, tuk-tuk, army truck and boat as LATER rows. Crossing zones by vehicle waits until multi-server travel works. Skateboard and kick scooter: no vehicle class; at most a rare joke item later.

verdicts.fact_check: The staging is internally consistent and the cited pattern exists: _shop_fronts appends last with its own rng (city_gen.gd:1180-1190, build order at 150-159). It inherits V06's inverted traffic-direction rule in Stage 0. It spends Stage 2 (1-2 weeks) re-rendering parked props with no gameplay change. It also makes the saleng depend on that renderer.
verdicts.reason: The ROADMAP rules are 'core loop first; systems that don't feed it wait' and 'one system at a time, each round playable' (lines 292, 296). A standalone box-renderer stage for parked cars feeds no loop, so it breaks the first rule. The plan also leaves out the maintenance loop (repair) that makes a player invest in a vehicle, and the ROADMAP already lists repair as next for bikes (line 229).
verdicts.revised_observation: The order is roughly right (cheap fixes and bicycle before cars). But it puts a pure-rendering stage before any gameplay, makes the saleng depend on it, and leaves out bike repair and fuel supply.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Stage 0 (S): parked-traffic fixes with the correct left-hand direction (V06), camera and headlight fixes (V13), bike repair plus wiring the existing ช่าง unlock to hotwire time (missed M1), fuel as litres in cans plus roadside bottled petrol (missed M2). Stage 1 (S-M): trunk and box search plus siphoning (V05), keys as items, and the bike kept indoors (V08). Stage 2 (S-M): bicycle (V09). Stage 3 (M): saleng drawn in BikeArt's own 4 views (V10). Stage 4, a decision gate: a 2-3 day box-model spike on wrecks only, with screenshots, then decide. If yes, build renderer + movement + seats + shelter as one round (V03, V11, V12, V04, V14). Later: tuk-tuk on LPG, army truck as a group objective, boat, crossing zones.

verdicts.fact_check: Correct. street_prop.gd:241-248: side view is an elevation with a 1.2-unit roof strip, top at -17 x 1.6 = about 27 px. 266-270: end view has a 26-unit top over a 5-unit face. building_prop.gd:154-164: facade rises h, roof = footprint at 1:1 lifted by h. Tuk-tuk and army truck each have one view (street_prop.gd:151-152, 198-199; city_gen.gd:986 forces tuk-tuks side-on). v17_bus_z4 right edge: the rotated side-on wreck does read as pitched nose-up. v12_taxi_z4 and v05 top: rotated end-on wrecks read as skidded. mesh_canvas.gd:30-53 applies any Transform2D. v16_songthaew_z4: the end-on songthaew is indeed a plain red slab.
verdicts.reason: Right direction for a drivable 4-wheeler: a rigid body at diagonal headings can't be done with 4 snapped views, and it stays in the buildings' own projection, so no new camera angle. The lens understates three costs. (1) Box cars get bigger on screen: a sedan side-on grows from about 27 px to about 48 px tall (22 roof depth + 26 height), and end-on from about 50 to about 79 px. That is the same 'tall things hide the street and the zombies in it' problem already found in today's city review. (2) For a beginner, remapping the current decals onto face affines, y-sorting long diagonal bodies (bus 147 px) and deriving roof_spot/roof_area/middle/_boxes/_low from data is closer to L than M. (3) It has no gameplay value until cars drive.
verdicts.revised_observation: Parked 4-wheelers mix a flat side elevation and an almost top-down end view, neither matching the buildings' projection. A rotated side view reads as the car pitching up, not skidding. That is fine for scenery but rules out 4 snapped views for a car you drive at diagonal headings.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Do not ship a renderer stage on its own. When the car is committed, first spend 2-3 days on a spike: VehicleArt with 2 boxes (body, cabin), the buildings' projection screen = (x, y - z), faces culled by outward normal, used only for wrecks. Compare screenshots at zoom 3-5 for readability and how much it hides. Keep heights low (car roof about 24-26 px) and fade a vehicle's top like roofs when the player is behind it. If the spike reads well, build the full data-driven version with the car. Until then, fix the existing art cheaply (V06).

verdicts.fact_check: Correct. zombie.gd:174 (ground bites skip riders), 189-195 (a lunge can grab or bite a rider: no riding check), 284-291 (bang the car of a player on its roof), actions.gd:61-89 (25% alarm once, 14 s, noise 380), vehicles.gd:206-226 (knock-down above 60 px/s, -3 bike hp). No closed-vehicle state exists.
verdicts.reason: 'A shelter zombies break into, not a tank' is the right fear model and reuses bang_car, alarm, grab and struggle without new zombie art. It only matters once cars exist, but it should be part of the car's definition from day one. A cheap version works now with parked cars and fits 'หนี (รถ หลังคา คลอง)' (ROADMAP line 393).
verdicts.revised_observation: Zombies already bang parked cars and set off alarms when someone stands on the roof, and they can grab a rider. Nothing yet models being inside a car: glass, doors, being pulled out.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: As proposed for the drivable car: glass hp per side, doors take 0.8 s and make noise, a broken side lets a lunging zombie grab the nearest occupant, zombies at the front slow the car, a horn works as a lure. Cheap version possible now: 'hide in a parked car' (E on car/taxi/van). The occupant is not drawn, or only a head. Zombies that saw you get in bang it with the existing bang_car (same alarm chance), glass breaks after N bangs, then the existing grab. It adds a second refuge beside roof climbing with no driving code.

verdicts.fact_check: Correct. interact.gd:106-108 and 219-223: the only street-car action is climbing. bike_art.gd:99-100 and 194-198: delivery boxes on extra<2 of wave/click/pcx are paint only. vehicles.gd:329-340: refuel only from 'fuelcan', electric returns early and nothing else recharges it. inventory.gd:17-26 and 93-99: 'box' refs index container_nodes (FurnitureProp, SIZE 8, furniture_prop.gd:6). One detail makes it worse than stated: a refuel consumes the whole jerrycan item (vehicles.gd:334; generator the same at things.gd:313), so no empty can is left to siphon into.
verdicts.reason: This is already in the ROADMAP (phase 2 'ค้นท้ายรถ บีบแตร ดูดน้ำมัน', phase 5 'ดูดน้ำมันจากซากรถ'). It feeds the core loop directly: avenues full of cars become a reason to take a risk. Seed-derived state, a saved diff and no GEN bump are all correct.
verdicts.revised_observation: The parked cars along every avenue are climbable scenery only. Fuel comes only from finding whole jerrycans, which are used up at once. Electric bikes can never be recharged.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: As proposed, with one change first: make petrol a liquid held in containers, reusing the Items fill/holds idea from core rule 2. A jerrycan holds 0-10 L and comes back empty after pouring, so a siphon has somewhere to go and a generator and a bike can share one can. Then add trunk/glovebox/delivery-box containers keyed by street_prop id (a small vehicle-container record, not a FurnitureProp), loot tables by kind, and siphoning (hose + container, 6 s, noise; taxis hold LPG). Also recharge electric bikes in buildings with power.

verdicts.fact_check: Items 2-4 are correct. Tuk-tuk always side-on: city_gen.gd:986; a 14x5 body with 2 wheels and no cab or bars: street_prop.gd:372-384; v13 x≈530-635 reads like the noodle cart. Army truck canvas top at -12 units (≈19 px) vs car roof ≈27 px (street_prop.gd:684, 248); v18 confirms it is lower than the player's head. Flip bar is 26 units on a 16-unit end car, with the no-op 'if side else' (street_prop.gd:459); v12 x≈770-920 confirms. Item 1 is half wrong. It is true that direction is fixed (side faces east, street_prop.gd:257-258; end faces south, 271-272) and that lanes carry no direction (city_gen.gd:921). But the proposed rule is for RIGHT-hand traffic. Thailand drives on the left: eastbound traffic keeps to the NORTH half and northbound traffic to the WEST half. The cited evidence v17_bus_z4 (bus and car in the north lanes facing east) actually shows CORRECT Thai lanes. v13's end-on blue car in the east half facing south is also correct. The lens's rule would turn every correct one backwards.
