verdicts.direction_check:
The overall direction is sound. Vehicles should differ by role, not by speed. Two-wheelers stay in the existing 4 views with the rider. A 4-wheeler can't be done with snapped views, so it needs the buildings' projection, with occupants hidden. The car should be a shelter zombies break into, not a tank. Cheap wins first. It respects every scope rule: no new character views, no camera rotation, no base building. The facts are mostly accurate and well cited.

What I would change:
(1) Fix a real error. The parked-traffic direction rule in V06, which V02 and V07 inherit, is written for right-hand traffic. Thailand drives on the left. North lanes face east and east lanes face south, and the cited v17 screenshot shows correctly placed vehicles.
(2) Don't front-load rendering. A standalone box-renderer stage for parked props feeds no loop, and the ROADMAP says core loop first and one playable system at a time. Put the car behind a decision gate with a 2-3 day spike. Also account for box cars being taller on screen (about 48 vs 27 px side-on), which worsens the known 'tall things hide the soi' problem.
(3) The near-term plan lacks the ownership and maintenance loop that makes a player invest in a vehicle: repair at the existing ซ่อมมอเตอร์ไซค์ shops, keys as items, fuel as litres from Thai sources (bottled petrol, coin pumps), and the bike parked inside the home. The home prefab already intends this ('the bike inside', data/prefabs/home.txt) but draws it as decor. This is the real bridge between the user's two topics, vehicles and living in buildings, and it answers the ROADMAP's own diagnosis that the game lacks 'something to want' (line 385).
(4) Decouple the saleng from the box renderer: draw its tray in BikeArt's 4 views.
(5) Treat crossing zones by vehicle as far-future, since server-to-server travel is untested.

With those changes the order becomes:
- S: fixes, repair and fuel.
- S-M: containers, siphon, keys and indoor parking.
- Bicycle.
- Saleng.
- Gated car round.

review.summary: Living indoors already has good bones: real shophouse layouts, a rooftop tank that rain fills, a stove that runs on the game clock, a loud shutter versus a quiet back door, and sleep that rewards a shut house. Four root causes make it feel off. (1) The 1 m collision grid is drawn exactly as it is: 42% of every shophouse ground floor is black 1 m wall, and doors stand upright in a flat plan (a wardrobe when shut, a pole when open), so homes read as blueprints. A drawing-only thin-wall pass fixes most of this with no rule or per-frame cost (mocked in life/home_*_thin_mock_z4.png). (2) The house is not a barrier for the senses: sound, smell, the sleep/wake radius and upstairs sight all ignore walls and floors, and 'safe' is judged for the whole building, even the bathroom door. (3) Security is upside down compared with a real Thai house: the steel shutter is the weakest door and can never be repaired, there is no inner line (no doors upstairs, no gate at the top of the stairs), and the roof is a vault zombies can never reach, so the best play is 'run to the roof', not 'hold your home'. (4) Every home is the same template, and several props look usable but are not (water jar, family bike, bulbs), so there is nothing to choose between. DIRECTION: keep the grid and the no-base-building rule, and make each home behave like a real Bangkok home in layers. The outer shell: a strong shutter and a weak back door, both repairable. The inner line: doors or a steel folding gate upstairs. The roof: an escape you close behind you, not a vault. Draw walls thin and let them stand between you and the dead. Then vary homes by features that matter for survival, in the prefab data, with a single GEN bump.
strengths: Real Bangkok shophouse logic in the plans: shop behind a 4-section rolling shutter, stairs mid-plot, back kitchen with a gas ring and red LPG tank, a food cupboard (ตู้กับข้าว), a squat toilet with the jar beside it, a Buddha shelf, shoes at the door (data/prefabs/README.txt, home.txt). Keep this as the reference for every new variant.
Neighbouring shophouses share one party wall, as real ones do (city_gen.gd _row). Plots are 1:1 metres inside, so a 4-cell room is a true 4 m.
The shutter is loud (NOISE_HIT) and rolls up or down as one piece, so the back door becomes the quiet way in and out. This is a real choice that comes out of the systems and costs nothing.

Water works the Bangkok way: taps draw from the rooftop tank, rain refills it (rain_total, nothing ticks every frame), and big buildings have a cistern plus a pump that needs generator power (buildings.gd).
The stove runs on the game clock (you can leave a pot), gas runs out after 2-6 uses, and the smell of cooking draws zombies (things.gd). This is the right model for 'use things at home'.
The sleep rules have the right intent: a shut-tight house heals 3x, a bed 1.5x, and a rotting corpse nearby spoils sleep (survival.gd). The claimed bed as your respawn point makes it your home.

Storeys are shown one floor at a time, the roof fades as you walk in, and clear stair labels (↑ ชั้น 2 / ↑ ดาดฟ้า) are visible in h03 and h05. Items stored in any cupboard persist, and stripping furniture for wood and nails, then boarding with it, closes a loop using only what is in the home.

Trade-specific interiors and loot (the gold shop's glass counters, safe and altar in h02) and big buildings laid out the Bangkok way (central corridor, stairs at both ends, a dead lift, zombies trapped inside in work clothes).

The drawing already hints at the fix: a closed door in a north-south wall is drawn as a thin 5 px leaf (door_prop.gd:105). The ground and upper floors are baked once into MeshCanvas meshes, so redrawing walls costs nothing per frame.

findings.title: Walls are drawn as 1 m black trenches: 42-51% of every home is wall
findings.observation: FACT: A wall cell (IWALL) is painted as a full dark 16 px cell (3a3632) with a 3 px lighter edge. The shophouse plan is 40 of 78 cells wall (51%). Across the 205 shophouses generated with seed 11, 8,258 of 19,532 ground-floor cells (42.3%) are IWALL. At zoom 4 the west wall of the plain home is about 63 screen px wide, about the same as the character (about 60 px). The same style is used upstairs and in the flats.
findings.evidence: world.gd:1127-1131 (IWALL drawn as a full cell plus a 3 px _edge); world.gd:288-305 (_draw_upper, same style); data/prefabs/home.txt; measurement script scratchpad/home_measure.gd ('wall cells 8258/19532 = 42.3%'). Screenshots: h04 (the black column at x 470-518 and the black band between the kitchen and the shop), h05/h07 (upstairs rooms boxed in by bands as wide as a person), h09/h10 (the flats corridor looks like a trench maze). Before and after: life/home_g_now_z4 vs home_g_thin_mock_z4, home_u_now_z4 vs home_u_thin_mock_z4, home_f_now_z4 vs home_f_thin_mock_z4 (a scratch overlay draws a 5 px wall on the wall line; collision unchanged).
findings.why: OPINION: Real block walls are 10-20 cm (2-3 px). A Thai shophouse feels long and open. The trench look is the biggest single reason rooms feel like corridors and a home looks like a floor-plan diagram instead of a place people lived. It is on screen every second you are indoors. The mock shows the same plan reading as real rooms at once.
findings.suggestion:
Keep the 1-cell collision and change only the drawing, with one helper used by both world.gd _draw_tile (IWALL) and _draw_upper:
- Draw a 5-6 px dark cap along the wall line: centred for partitions and party walls, and on the room side for outer walls (draw the outside ground right up to it).
- Add a 3 px lighter 'face' under walls that run across the screen.
- Paint the rest of the cell as the neighbouring floor.

Follow-ups:
- Nudge furniture and decor that stand against a wall 4-5 px toward it. This is a draw offset only, in FurnitureProp/DecorProp, when the neighbouring cell is IWALL. The mock shows them floating otherwise.
- Draw the upstairs windows inside the band.

What it breaks: no rule changes. sight_ray, astar, path_on and can_stand stay cell-based, and nobody stands in a wall cell.
- Visual: you stop about 4 px short of a thin partition. With outer walls drawn on the outside edge you would stop about 10 px short, which is why outer walls go on the room side.
- Doors in walls must be restyled (L2).
findings.scope_check: No character views involved. Pure drawing. Ground chunks and upper floors are baked once into MeshCanvas, so there is zero per-frame cost. Tiles are unchanged, so no CityGen.GEN bump.

findings.title: Doors stand upright in a flat plan: a wardrobe when shut, a pole when open
findings.observation: FACT: Doors in walls that run across the screen are drawn 15 px tall and stretched 2x to 30 px, standing up in the wall cell. When open they shrink to a 2.5 px x 30 px strip. Interior doors ('d') are generated open, so every house shows 'poles'. The walls around them are drawn flat. Doors in north-south walls are already drawn as a flat 5 px leaf.
findings.evidence: door_prop.gd:6-8 (DOOR_STRETCH 2.0); door_prop.gd:56-60 (open = 2.5 px wide); door_prop.gd:105-108 (side door = 5 px leaf); world.gd:158-161; city_gen.gd:505-508 (interior doors forced open). Screenshots: h03 (the open kitchen door is the brown pole at x~528, y 420-570; the bathroom door stands like a wardrobe over the jar and toilet at x 640-700); art_01 (the back door and bathroom door of the house across the soi stand up like cupboards); 20_hospital_ground (a pole at every room doorway); home_g_thin_mock_z4 (with thin walls the pole and the upright doors look even more out of place).
findings.why: OPINION: Doors are the home object you use most (open, close, board, repair). If they don't read as doors, securing the house feels abstract. Mixing top-down walls with upright doors is a big part of why a correct layout still looks 'off'.
findings.suggestion:
When the roof is off, draw doors the way a floor plan does, as the north-south door already is:
- Closed: a 5 px leaf filling the doorway inside the thin wall band (L1).
- Open: the leaf swung against the jamb as a 5x14 px strip on the room side, with a faint quarter-arc.
- Boards: short planks across the leaf. Broken: splinters.

Keep today's upright 3/4 drawing for the front door, back door and shutters when seen from outside (roof on). DoorProp can choose the style from door.side and whether its building is Main.hidden_building. The simplest version is to always draw interior 'd' doors in plan style.
findings.scope_check: Drawing in one file. DoorProp only redraws when a door changes state. No new views, no GEN bump.

findings.title: The steel shutter is the weakest door in the house and can never be repaired
findings.observation: FACT: A shutter section has 150 HP and cannot be boarded. The only actions on a shutter are open and close. A wooden back door with 3 boards reaches 60+180 = 240 HP. A normal zombie hits a door for 12 every 1.1 s: a shutter section falls in about 14 s, and in about 5 s to a fat zombie (door x3). Glass takes 1 hit. Once a section is broken it stays open for good: there is no repair or board action for a broken shutter, zombies walk through, and spot_safe will never call that house shut tight again. It already happens at generation: 15% of lowered shutters start prised open (11 of 96 in seed 11). Anyone can also roll a shutter up from the street, although the code comment says it is padlocked from inside.
findings.evidence: world.gd:16-21 (DOOR_HP 60, WINDOW_HP 15, SHUTTER_HP 150, BOARD_HP 60, MAX_BOARDS 3); interact.gd:166-172 (shutter: open/close only, nothing when broken); zombie.gd:9-21 and 445-457 (door multipliers, 12 dmg per 1.1 s); city_gen.gd:529-541 (the 'padlocked from inside' comment, pried 15%); survival.gd:91-104; survival.gd:379 (the horde warning tells you 'ปิดประตู ตอกไม้ให้แน่น'). Latent bug: doors.gd:84 uses DOOR_HP as base_hp for shutters, and doors.gd:77-79 repairs to DOOR_HP. Measurement: 11 pried of 96 lowered shutters, 205 shophouses.
findings.why: OPINION: In Bangkok, a steel shutter padlocked from inside is the strongest thing a shophouse has, and the back door is the weak point. Inverting this means the front falls first on horde nights, the thing the game tells you to board can't be boarded, and a house whose shutter was broken once is worthless as a home forever. That works against 'choose where to live and look after it'.
findings.suggestion:
Numbers and one action branch:
- SHUTTER_HP 150 → about 400-600 per section, the strongest opening. Cap the fat zombie's door multiplier on steel at about 1.5.
- Allow R on a broken section: 'ปิดช่องด้วยไม้' (1-3 boards, BOARD_HP each). It becomes closed and can't be rolled up until the boards are prised off.
- Fix doors.gd:77-86 so shutters use SHUTTER_HP as their base. Otherwise, boarding a shutter would lower it from 150 to 120.
- Later (Phase 2 'กุญแจ'): padlocked from inside means it can only be opened from inside.

Keep the loud noise. Also keep the idea that fixing it takes effort (wood from stripped furniture).
findings.scope_check: Numbers plus one branch in Interact and Doors. DoorProp already draws boards and broken shutters. No views, no GEN bump, no per-frame cost.

findings.title: Safe sleep is judged for the whole building and ignores walls and floors
findings.observation: FACT: spot_safe needs every door and window in the building shut. That includes interior doors, which are generated open, so you must also close the bathroom and kitchen doors to get the 3x 'shut tight' heal. The message only says 'doors/windows are open'. In a flats or office block that means 16-27 ground-floor openings (7-14 open at start) plus every trapped zombie on every floor (11-14 per big building) dealt with. 'Can't sleep' (120 px, about 7.5 cells) and 'wake up' (70 px) use plain distance, ignoring walls, shut shutters and storeys. Shophouses are 13-15 cells deep and sois are 3 cells wide, so most beds have street within 7.5 cells.
findings.evidence: survival.gd:82-89 (_nearest_zombie, straight-line distance); survival.gd:91-104 (spot_safe checks every door of the building); survival.gd:107-116 and 145-152 (SLEEP_TOO_CLOSE, SLEEP_WAKE); city_gen.gd:505-508; city_gen.gd:28, 58-59 (SOI_W 3, depth 13-15). Measurement: 'BIG flats ... windows 4-14, inner doors 4-8, openings not shut at start 7-14, trapped 11-14'.
findings.why: OPINION: Sleeping at home is the reward step of the core loop. If the rule doesn't match what the player sees ('I shut the shutter and the back door and went upstairs'), it feels arbitrary. Real people sleep through zombies shuffling outside a steel shutter; they wake to banging.
findings.suggestion:
1) Judge 'shut tight' per enclosure. Flood-fill the floor from the sleeper through open doorways on that storey (CityGen already builds rec.rooms), and check only the openings on the edge of that region plus the stairwell (later the stair gate, L5). Interior doors inside the region don't count.
2) 'Can't sleep' and 'wake up' should only count a zombie that can reach you without passing a shut door (the same flood-fill, or at least same building and same storey). Also wake anyone asleep whose enclosure contains a door that Doors.damage_door is hitting, so banging wakes you.
3) Make the message name the open opening ('ประตูหลังยังเปิด').

Keep the corpse-smell rule.
findings.scope_check: Server logic only, run once a second per sleeper. Rooms are known at generation. No drawing, no views, no GEN bump.

findings.title: No inner line of defence: no doors upstairs, and the roof is a vault
findings.observation: FACT: Floors above the ground have no doors. A plan's 'd' becomes open floor, and doors have no storey (World.doors is keyed by cell; Interact lists no doors upstairs). Zombies never pick a target on another floor. They only follow you up the stairs if they were already chasing you and within 160 px. Zombies can never reach the roof ('ซอมบี้ตามขึ้นมาไม่ได้'). Roofs join along a row, so from any roof you can walk to the next and take any house's stairs down.
findings.evidence: city_gen.gd:438 and 450-452 (upstairs 'd' → FLOOR, 'Doorways up here are open'); interact.gd:44-57 (upstairs candidates: no doors); zombie.gd:202-204 (the 160 px follow) and zombie.gd:515 (no targets on another storey); actions.gd:298; world.gd:897-900 (joined roofs); h05, h07 and home_u_now_z4 (upstairs doorways are gaps).
findings.why: OPINION: In a real Thai shophouse, the fallback is upstairs behind a door, or behind a steel folding gate (ประตูเหล็กยืด) at the top of the stairs, with the roof door as the last way out. Here the ladder is: a weak ground floor, then nothing, then an invulnerable roof. So on horde nights the best play is 'run to the roof'. That makes boarding and looking after the house optional, and removes the 'hold the house' tension the ROADMAP wants ('คืนฝูงบุกมุ่งไปบ้านที่มีคน').
findings.suggestion:
Give doors a storey: a 'storey' key on the door, a per-storey door_at (like storeys_blocked), is_solid_on checks it, zombies' closed_door_near and bashing filter by storey, and DoorProp joins b.storey_nodes. Door ids stay global, so saves and the door_state RPC keep working.

Then in the plans:
- Upstairs 'd' become real wooden doors.
- All 52 letters are taken, so add a symbol: '=' for a steel folding gate (strong, doesn't block sight, fairly quiet), usable at the top of the stairs.
- Add '+' for the roof door on the top stair cell.

Roof: zombies already chasing you may follow you up the stairs unless the roof door is shut. The roof stays an escape (you can shut it behind you and still jump down, as the ROADMAP lists roofs as a way to flee), but it stops being a free vault. The Phase 2 item 'ลากเฟอร์นิเจอร์' (pushing a cupboard across the stair head) fits here too without base building. A shut stair gate is also what makes a 'safe floor' for L4.
findings.scope_check: Uses existing doors and views, with a data/system extension. DoorProp only redraws on state change. The new plan letters need a CityGen.GEN bump: do it together with L7, L11 and L13 so the city resets once.

findings.title: Every home is the same home
findings.observation: FACT: All 11 shophouse plans have exactly the same first 6 rows (kitchen, bathroom, back door, dividing wall), and 10 of 11 have exactly the same upstairs (the clinic moves one row). Only the 5-7 front rows differ by trade. 56 of 205 shophouses (27%) use home.txt. The 4x3 middle room upstairs holds only the stairs. So in all 205 houses the tap, stove, fridge, jar, stairs and beds are in the same place, and every house has one back door, two single beds and the same flat roof.
findings.evidence: data/prefabs/*.txt (a diff: 'distinct back halves: 2 (all shophouses + minimart), distinct upstairs: 3'); measurement 'SIGNS { "": 56, ... }'; city_gen.gd:385-394 (one plan per trade). Screenshots: h03/h04 (gold shop), 17/18 (another shop) and home_g_now_z4 (plain home) show the same kitchen; h05, 19 and home_u_now_z4 show the same upstairs.
findings.why: OPINION: The game's promise is 'เลือกที่อยู่เอง' (choose where to live), and later one claimed home per person or group. A choice needs differences that matter for survival: a steel folding gate, a balcony over the street, rain jars in a back yard, a third floor, no back door (one way in: safer, but a trap), an upstairs bathroom with a tap. With one template, homes differ only in loot and location, so 'home' just means the nearest bed.
findings.suggestion:
Split each plan into parts that the generator combines, all as data:
- A front per trade, as now.
- A back, 3-4 variants: kitchen with a back door to the soi; a walled-in back with no door (row backs onto a row); a back yard with jars and a clothes line; a back door behind a steel gate ('=').
- The stairs: in the middle, or along the party wall like real shophouses (which frees the middle).
- An upstairs: 2 bedrooms; a front room with a balcony over the street; a Buddha room plus bathroom; or a real 3rd floor for the 3-storey facades (this also fixes the known facade mismatch).

Add README entries like 'part: back', pick parts by building seed, and give each variant one survival trait the player can read ('หลังบ้านมีโอ่ง', 'มีระเบียง'). Also vary small things by seed: a 2-cell family bed, whether there is a fan, where the fridge stands.
findings.scope_check: Mostly prefab text plus a small combiner in CityGen._build_plan. Existing letters and views. One GEN bump, shared with L5, L11 and L13. No per-frame cost.

findings.title: You can't look out: the ground floor is blind and upstairs sees everything
findings.observation: FACT: Sight is switched off upstairs, on the roof and while asleep. So from floor 2 every zombie outside your building is shown, even through windowless party walls and other buildings. On the ground floor with the shutter down you see only 26 px around you. The upper floor has 2-3 windows in the front and back walls, but they do nothing. Below them, the front is drawn as a solid slab of wall colour.
findings.evidence: sight.gd:28 ('want := ... me.storey == 0 and not me.sleeping  # (upstairs, you look out of the windows)'); sight.gd:13 (NEAR 26); main.gd:1168-1173 (_on_view_floor only hides your own building's ground floor); world.gd:284-285 (the slab) and world.gd:303-305 (window cells); h07 (the lilac slab at y 455-575 under the two windows); h05.
findings.why: OPINION: Knowing what's outside is the key decision at home: go out now, or wait? In a shophouse you check from the upstairs front window or through the steel folding gate. Here you either know nothing or everything, and it doesn't depend on where you stand, so windows, the front room and gates have no role.
findings.suggestion:
Upstairs: keep sight on.
- If you stand within about 2 cells of a window cell on your floor, the eye moves to that window and looks outward: a 150° cone with full reach. Share one function, upper_windows(rec), with the drawing.
- Otherwise you see only your own floor and building.

Ground floor:
- A closed shutter lets you see about 3 cells through its gaps.
- A steel folding gate ('=', L5/L6) doesn't block sight; glass already doesn't.

Roof: keep full sight (you are on top).

Also replace the slab under the upper floor with the awning and sign seen from above, so the window looks out onto the street. Do not use a darkening shade (rejected before); hiding out-of-sight characters is the existing mechanism.
findings.scope_check: Sight already casts about 100 rays a frame; this only changes where the eye is, so the per-frame budget is the same. No new views, no GEN bump.

findings.title: Night at home is dark and you can't choose to make light
findings.observation: FACT: Room bulbs light only when the building has power, and only big buildings have generators ('เครื่องปั่นไฟพกพา/ตึกแถว' is not done). So the one-bulb-per-room in every shophouse never lights. The only light item is the headlamp. Light already matters to zombies: a lit player is seen from daylight range.
findings.evidence: world.gd:482-500 (_bulb_on, is_lit need power); city_gen.gd:609-610 (a bulb per room); data/items.cfg:1719 (ไฟฉายคาดหัว is the only light); zombie.gd:520 (lit → SIGHT_DAY); ROADMAP 'แกนกลาง' round 4 'ยังไม่ทำ'.
findings.why: OPINION: In Bangkok blackouts, every home reaches for candles and a rechargeable emergency lamp (ไฟฉุกเฉิน). Light at home should be a choice with a price: see to cook, craft and feel safe, versus windows glowing and zombies spotting you from far away. That is the kind of 'systems collide' decision the ROADMAP section 'หาความสนุก' asks for, built from parts that already exist.
findings.suggestion:
New item rows: เทียนไข (burns about 3 game hours), ตะเกียงน้ำมัน (uses fuel), ไฟฉุกเฉิน (uses ถ่านไฟฉาย).
- F sets one down, like a trap, as a Thing 'lamp' with state {on, until} on the game clock (like the stove).
- While it's lit:
  - add a light spot tagged with the building id, so is_lit works for zombies' eyes;
  - reuse the bulb PointLight2D texture;
  - set the building's lit-window glow (BuildingProp.glow already draws lit windows when data.lit), so it shows from the street.
- Where to find them: candles at the Buddha shelf 'I' and the altar 'a' (where Thais keep them); emergency lamps in homes and minimarts.
findings.scope_check: Item rows plus one Thing kind that reuses the stove's clock state, the bulb light and the window glow. Only a few PointLight2Ds (one per lit lamp). No views, no GEN bump (players place them).

findings.title: Flats and condos can't be a home yet
findings.observation: FACT: Flat units above the ground floor have no door (L5) and no bathroom. Safety is judged for the whole block: 16-27 ground-floor openings (7-14 open at start) and 11-14 trapped zombies spread over every floor. The good parts are already there: taps on 95% of floors, a large roof tank plus a cistern and a pump that needs power, stairs at both ends, a dead lift.
findings.evidence: big_plans.gd:52-117 (corridor plan; 'd' on every floor, 'w' only on the ground) and 231-242 (unit furnishing); things.gd:445-447 (taps upstairs 95%); buildings.gd:64-97; survival.gd:91-104; measurement 'BIG flats (29,16) floors 7 ... trapped 14' and similar; h09 (ten doorless units on one floor).
findings.why: OPINION: The ROADMAP plans 'คอนโดแบ่งเป็นห้อง ๆ (ตึกเดียวอยู่ได้หลายครอบครัว)'. A high flat is the most realistic safe home in Bangkok (zombies must climb 5-7 floors, and there is one door to hold), and the natural shared home for 20-50 players per zone. Today it is a maze of doorless rooms you can never secure.
findings.suggestion:
Once doors have a storey (L5):
- Give every unit a door on every floor, and some a steel folding gate.
- Enclosure-based safety (L4) makes 'my unit is shut' count.
- Each floor's stair head can get a fire door.
- Vary the units (L11).

When claiming arrives, let a claim own a unit (a room in rec.rooms) rather than a whole building.
findings.scope_check: Builds on L4 and L5. Plan data plus the enclosure logic. GEN bump shared. No views.

findings.title: Walls don't muffle anything: noise and smell ignore the house
findings.observation: FACT: Main.stimulus reaches every zombie inside the radius. Only a different storey halves it, and rain covers it; walls and shut doors do nothing. A radio (95 px), cooking smell (110), hammering boards (90), the shutter (130) and the generator (190) carry just as far from a sealed house as from the street. ROADMAP core item 4 says 'ฝนกลบ ผนังกั้น' (rain covers, walls block); only the rain part is done.
findings.evidence: main.gd:663-684 (stimulus: storey and rain only); things.gd:35-39 (COOK_SMELL, RADIO_NOISE, GEN_NOISE); doors.gd _reinforce (NOISE_SWING when hammering); ROADMAP.md 'แกนกลาง' item 4.
findings.why: OPINION: Cooking, boiling water, boarding up and listening to the radio are the most home-like actions. If doing them behind a shut door costs exactly the same as in the street, the house gives them no shelter and shutting up has no payoff.
findings.suggestion: In stimulus: if the source is inside a building and the zombie is not in that building, multiply the radius by about 0.5 when the building is shut and about 0.75 when it is open (smell: 0.6 and 0.85). Reuse the L4 enclosure test, cached per building and refreshed when a door changes. Loud things (generator, shutter) stay loud because their base radius is large. Mirror it for a zombie indoors hearing noise from outside.
findings.scope_check: One server function plus a cache that updates on door changes. No drawing, no views, no GEN bump.

findings.title: Objects that don't fit their room: shop coolers at home, toilets beside beds, empty middle rooms
findings.observation:
FACT:
- The 'fridge' is always drawn as a glass-door drinks cooler with coloured bottles, including in every home kitchen and every flat unit.
- Flat units put the squat toilet, tap and sink in the open bedroom with no partition, and every unit on a floor gets the same 8 items.
- Every shophouse's upstairs middle room is 4x3 cells holding only the stairs.
- Hospital and office rooms are furnished only along the far wall ('the row by the door stays clear'), leaving large empty floors.
findings.evidence: furniture_prop.gd:139-145 (the fridge drawing); big_plans.gd:231-242 (unit: b,b,c,v,n,f,K,T,q); big_plans.gd _furnish; home.txt floor 2 rows 5-7. Screenshots: h03 (the cooler in the kitchen); h09, h10 and home_f_now_z4 (a cooler and a toilet plate next to the bed in every unit); h05 and home_u_now_z4 (the empty middle room); 20_hospital_ground (rooms 10+ cells wide with 3-4 items along one wall).
findings.why: OPINION: These are what you notice the moment you walk in. They say 'generated' rather than 'someone lived here', and they work against the realism-first goal.
findings.suggestion:
- FurnitureProp: draw a 'fridge' in a home (table 'home') as a Thai home fridge: opaque 1-2 doors, white or pastel, magnets, a water bottle on top. Keep the cooler for shops.
- Flat unit: a 2x2 walled bathroom (with an open doorway) in the corner by the corridor, holding q, T and a jar. Put the sink on a back balcony strip, which also gives a window to look out of (L7).
- Vary units by seed: student room, family (double bed, shrine shelf), older couple (rice cooker, clothes rack).
- Shophouse middle room: a Buddha room or storage (I, boxes, clothes rack), or run the stairs along the wall (L6).
- Hospital rooms: add a second row (chairs, desk, curtain rails) so rooms have a middle.
findings.scope_check: The fridge look is drawing only (no GEN bump). The plan and furnishing changes are data but need the shared GEN bump. No new views.

findings.title: The water jar and other home props look usable but aren't
findings.observation: FACT: The water jar (โอ่ง, 'J') is dressing that blocks its cell. Taps draw from the rooftop tank and stop working until it rains ('แท็งก์บนดาดฟ้าแห้ง · รอฝน'). Also decoration only: the squat toilet, TV, fan, spirit house, Buddha shelf, and the family motorbike in the living room (see L13).
findings.evidence: city_gen.gd:60-68 (J = 'jar' in DECOR_BLOCKS, not a Thing); things.gd:16-29 (DEFS has no jar) and things.gd:54-57 (dry tap); buildings.gd:69-76 (tank); ROADMAP 'ที่อยู่ในโลกออนไลน์': 'ประปาหยุด (ต้องมีแท็งก์/รองน้ำฝน/อยู่ใกล้คลอง)'.
findings.why: OPINION: The jar is exactly the Thai answer to 'the tap has stopped', and the ROADMAP expects rain collection to decide which home can last. Props that look usable but do nothing make the home feel like a stage set.
findings.suggestion:
Make 'J' a Thing 'jar' in things.gd DEFS: holds about 40 sips and starts with some water (seeded).
- Indoors: you fill it from the tap or from bottles, as a store for when the tank runs dry.
- Outdoors (the back-yard or roof variants in L6): it fills from rain the same way the tank does (rain_total, no ticking).
- Drinking straight from it is 'unboiled' like canal water, at lower risk. You can scoop it into bottles or a pot.

Leave the TV, fan and toilet as decoration until power and heat systems exist. Don't add systems that don't feed the core loop.
findings.scope_check: One Thing kind reusing the tank's rain model and the tap's actions. The jar is already drawn. No views. Outdoor jars come with the L6 plan variants (shared GEN bump); indoor jars need none.

findings.title: Your motorbike can't come home with you (links vehicles and homes)
findings.observation: FACT: Vehicles cannot enter FLOOR or DOOR cells, so bikes stay in the street. Meanwhile the home and bike-shop plans put a decoration-only motorbike ('e') in the living room that can't be used.
findings.evidence: world.gd:821 and 889 (road flag: FLOOR/DOOR are solid for vehicles); data/prefabs/home.txt row 11 'We.jRW'; bikeshop.txt ('e'); city_gen.gd:62-63 (e = decor 'bike').
findings.why: OPINION: Wheeling the motorbike into the shophouse at night and pulling the shutter down is universal Thai practice. Linking the two systems gives your bike a home, gives the shutter something to guard, and makes the bike inside a shuttered house a reason to break in. The two parts of the user's question become one loop.
findings.suggestion:
- Let a vehicle cross FLOOR/DOOR cells only at CRAWL speed (vehicles.gd), through an open shutter group or a double doorway, and park inside on the ground floor. It stops at furniture as it does at walls.
- At generation, turn the 'e' decoration into a real parked vehicle via Vehicles.setup, with the key in a cabinet or missing.
- Riding indoors uses the existing ride poses and the bike's 4 views.
findings.scope_check: Existing views and rig. Logic change in slide/can_stand for the road flag. The 'e' conversion needs the shared GEN bump. One more bike near a player is negligible per frame.

findings.title: Root causes and the order to fix them
findings.observation:
The 13 findings above come from 4 causes:
(1) The collision grid is drawn as-is: 1 m top-down walls next to upright 3/4 doors, furniture and people (L1, L2).
(2) The building is a solid shape but not a barrier for the senses: sound, smell, sleep and upstairs sight ignore walls and floors, and safety is judged for the whole building (L4, L7, L10).
(3) Security is modelled on generic doors instead of the real Thai house: the strong shutter is weak and can't be repaired, there is no inner line, and the roof is invulnerable (L3, L5, L9).
(4) One template per home, and props that look usable but aren't, so there is nothing to choose between and little to 'use' at home (L6, L8, L11, L12, L13).
findings.evidence: See L1-L13. All numbers come from the code lines and the seed-11 measurements cited there. Before/after images: life/home_*_now_z4 vs home_*_thin_mock_z4.
findings.why: OPINION: The user's 'ขัดๆ' feeling indoors isn't one bug. The look (cause 1) is what you notice first. Causes 2 and 3 are why shutting yourself in doesn't feel like being safe at home, and cause 4 is why no home feels like yours.
findings.suggestion:
Order:
1) Quick S fixes this week, no GEN bump: L3 (shutter HP, board a broken section), L4 (enclosure-based sleep and waking), L10 (muffling).
2) The drawing pass, no GEN bump: L1 thin walls plus L2 doors drawn in plan style, and the home fridge look from L11. Check it with the scratch mock first.
3) One GEN bump bundling: L5 doors with a storey, stair gate '=' and roof door '+'; L6 home variants; the L11 plan fixes; L13 'e' as real bikes.
4) L7 sight from the windows, L8 lamps, L12 the jar.
5) L9 flats as homes, when home claiming starts.

Rule of thumb for every change: the house should stand between you and the dead, in layers you can see and maintain.
findings.scope_check: Every step stays inside the scope rules. No new character views or camera angles. No base building: only doors, gates and furniture that are generated with the city. Mostly data and logic, with drawing baked once. The city resets only once (step 3).

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. world.gd:1127-1131 paints IWALL as a full cell in COLORS[IWALL] 3a3632 (world.gd:42) with a 3 px 6e665c edge toward FLOOR (_edge, world.gd:1015). _draw_upper (world.gd:279-305) uses the same full-cell wall. home.txt floor 2 is 40/78 wall (51%); the ground floor is 35/78 (45%), so the '51%' figure is the upstairs plan. A cell is 64 screen px at zoom 4, the same as a band in home_g_now_z4. The thin mocks (home_g/u/f_thin_mock_z4) do read as real rooms. They also show the tradeoffs the finding admits: the fridge floats off the west wall, the open door is a pole, and the upstairs E-W caps sit mid-cell. Collision: Player.RADIUS 5 and FOOT_DEPTH 0.4 (world.gd:869-873). Beside a centred 5 px N-S partition the player's feet stop about 5.5 px short of the cap (about 22 screen px at z4). North of a centred E-W wall, the feet stop about 7.5 px short, and in 3/4 view the body does not cover that gap.
verdicts.reason: The diagnosis is right and the direction (drawing only, collision unchanged, baked into MeshCanvas) is sound.
