verdicts.direction_check:
The lens's direction is sound. Keep the 1 m grid and the no-base-building rule, and make the house stand between you and the dead in layers you can see and maintain. It is evidence-based, and almost every fact checks out in code and screenshots. Two facts are wrong or overstated:
- L2 says N-S doors are already flat. They are flat only when shut; open side doors stand 28 px tall and are the 'wardrobe' in h03.
- L3's 'weakest door' is only true after boarding (150 vs 60 unboarded).

What I would change:
(1) Put all cheap, no-GEN, S items first. That is L4, L3 and L10, plus the L11 home-fridge look and the L12 jar, which can use the existing Things.place_stoves pattern with no GEN bump.
(2) Treat L1 as a prototype-then-ship pass together with L2 and the furniture nudges, using 3/4-aware wall placement: E-W caps at the north edge of their cell with a face. Otherwise the 'black trench' becomes 'invisible walls and floating props'. A plaster-coloured full-cell wall is the fallback.
(3) L5 as written ('doors get a storey') is an L refactor for a beginner. Reach the same layers more cheaply:
- a per-stairwell stair-head barrier and roof hatch (state like the tank);
- furniture barricades through the existing BUILDS structures and damage_door (Phase 2 'ลากเฟอร์นิเจอร์').
Also close the roof-sleep loophole. Present 'zombies may follow onto the roof' to the user as a choice, because it reverses an announced mechanic.
(4) Vary homes per ROW (one developer, one plan), plus per-unit renovations, rather than random parts per unit. That is truer to Bangkok and bundles with the real floor 3.
(5) Merge L9 into L5 and L4.
(6) Add the missing layer of 'why go home': sleep has no pull, and online the night can't be skipped. Without it, much of the sleep and safety work goes unused.
The lens barely covers the vehicle half of the user's question (only L13). That is fine if another lens owns vehicles, but L13 must keep the 'never in shop fronts or doorways' parking rule.

review.summary: Seen through the living lens, what feels off comes from two root causes. First, every home is the same self-sufficient box: 11 of 12 shophouse plans share the same back half, every roof tank refills about three times over in one shower, every kitchen has a working gas stove and the beds are always upstairs. Second, the walls of a home change almost nothing. Sound and smell pass through walls, the 'safe' check counts the toilet door, upper floors have no doors, and every roof is a room zombies can never reach. So home is a sleep bonus and a respawn point, not a place you chose and have to keep. Recommended direction: treat a home as (a) walls that leak sound, smell, light and air depending on how shut it is, plus (b) a few supplies that differ between buildings and run down as the days pass. Water goes mains, then tank, then jars or canal; cooking fuel is a scarce gas bottle or a smoky charcoal stove; light is candles and lamps; power is the generator. Each is a small Things/Buildings/Body.CONDITIONS entry that collides with the existing stimulus, door, rain and generator systems, and a one-line home appraisal makes the choice readable. Build it in 4 rounds: (1) walls + roof, (2) supplies, (3) nights at home, (4) claiming, online and condo units. Settle the game-clock scale first so home jobs don't take 5 seconds. Explicitly do NOT do: base building or free furniture dragging (only bracing an existing door with furniture already in that room), meters for tiredness/bladder/hygiene/morale, temperature simulation, decorating, or any new character view.
strengths: Shophouse plans follow real Bangkok layouts: shop at the front behind a rolling steel shutter, stairs mid-plot, back kitchen with gas stove + red bottle, water jar (โอ่ง), squat toilet and back door, bedrooms with a stand fan and chest of drawers upstairs (data/prefabs/home.txt; screenshots h03, h04, h05, 19_shop_upstairs). Keep and extend; don't replace.

The rolling shutter is loud and opens all at once (doors.gd:145-159, NOISE_HIT 130), while the back door is quiet. That already gives a real 'which entrance do I use' choice, and it's the kind of collision the design wants.
The generator is a model system: fuel on the game clock, lights, fridges, the water pump, and a loud noise that draws zombies (things.gd:26-31, 288-363). A single object creates a real trade-off.

Timestamp state (Buildings tank/power runs, Things 'ready', food 'made' + Items.chill) means nothing ticks per frame. New home systems (jars, lamps, charcoal, mains by day) can be added at no per-frame cost.
Adding a thing is cheap: Things.DEFS + actions_for + _do_kind_verb, with storey support and WorldState saving/syncing. Jar, lamp, charcoal stove and roof door each fit in about a page of code.
Body.CONDITIONS with mods is the right place for heat, rest, mosquitoes and calm effects without adding new meters. The mongkol already shows 'belief as a small real effect' (survival.gd:238).

Boil-your-water realism: tap water 6% sick, canal water 45% sick, boiled water clean (items.gd:511-515). Cooking smell draws zombies (things.gd:353-354), and a rotting body nearby ruins your sleep (survival.gd:142-167). These small, true details collide with other systems.
Big buildings are a prize you pay for: 2-14 trapped zombies on every floor, removed for good only when killed (buildings.gd:37-46, survival.gd:501-590).

The Thai texture is right: spirit houses on the sois (h01 left), Chinese altar, safe and glass gold counters in the gold shop (h02), Buddha shelf, barred and boarded facade windows, rooftop tanks and AC units (h08).
Claimed bed = respawn, plus a bigger sleep heal inside a building that is shut tight: the seed of 'home' is already there and easy to build on.

findings.title: The house shell does nothing: sound and smell pass through walls, 'safe' counts inner doors, floors barely matter
findings.observation: Main.stimulus uses straight-line distance only. Its only modifiers are rain (sound x0.65, smell x0.4) and OTHER_FLOOR 0.5 for any different storey. So cooking smell (110 px every 5 s), the generator (190), a radio (95) and hammering boards (90) carry exactly as far with the shutter down as with it up. Survival.spot_safe needs every door inside the building's rect closed, including interior doorways (the home plan has a kitchen doorway and a toilet door on the ground floor, both generated open), and it fails if any zombie is anywhere in the building on any storey. OTHER_FLOOR is flat, so a 7th-floor flat is as audible as the 2nd floor.
findings.evidence: main.gd:671-684 (SENSES, OTHER_FLOOR, stimulus loop: no wall/door test); ROADMAP core 4 lists 'ผนังกั้น' but it isn't implemented; things.gd:35,38-39,353-363; doors.gd:92; survival.gd:91-104 (all doors in building_at == b; zombies with building_at == b, any storey); world.gd:143-145 (building_at covers the whole rect); city_gen.gd:505-508 ('d' = door, opened); data/prefabs/home.txt rows 'WG.dqW' and 'WWdWWW'.
findings.why: The difference between inside and outside is the core feeling of a home. Right now the walls are a yes/no switch for the sleep bonus and transparent for everything else. 'Pull the shutter down before cooking' and 'live high up' aren't real decisions. And the safe icon failing because the toilet door is open feels like a bug. Fact: the code above. Opinion: this is the single hinge that most other home systems (light, heat, generator, cooking) need to collide with.
findings.suggestion: (a) spot_safe: count only openings on the building's outer edge (a door cell on the rect border, or next to a cell outside the building). In big buildings, only count zombies on your storey or ±1. (b) Cache a per-building 'shell' level, updated in Doors.door_state: 0 = some outer opening open or broken, 1 = all shut, 2 = all shut and every window boarded / shutter down. (c) In stimulus: when the source and the zombie are on opposite sides of a building's shell, radius *= [1.0, 0.55, 0.4][shell]. An open back door or window lets smell out at full strength. (d) Replace the flat 0.5 per floor with radius / (1 + |storey difference|). (e) Say it once in the status line: 'ปิดบ้านครบ · เสียงข้างในเล็ดลอดออกไปน้อย'. No GEN bump.
findings.scope_check: No character views, no art. A pure system change in main.gd, survival.gd and doors.gd. Per stimulus: one building lookup for the source plus one per zombie in range (a dictionary read). Nothing is redrawn. Save format unchanged (the cache is rebuilt from doors).

findings.title: Every roof is a room zombies can never reach, so the home never has to hold
findings.observation: Zombies ignore any player with on_roof: they won't grab, lunge, follow up the stairs or pick a roof player as a target. The status even says 'บนดาดฟ้า · ซอมบี้ขึ้นมาไม่ได้'. Every shophouse roof is reachable by its stairs (h08: a '↓บันได' hatch on every roof). Horde zombies spawn around a player and head for them. Once you're on a roof, they have nothing left to do.
findings.evidence: zombie.gd:174, 189, 202 (no climb after an on_roof target), 515 (_nearest_player skips on_roof); body.gd:328-329; survival.gd:389-400 (_spawn_horde_zombie); interact.gd:65-69 (on the roof only the stairs and the roof edge are in reach); screenshot h08_on_roof_z3 (hatches on each roof).
findings.why: The most realistic tension of a home (will the door hold on horde night, the last retreat upstairs) is short-circuited: the best answer to any siege is 'go up'. Real shophouse roofs are reached through a door or hatch at the top of the stairs. People bar it, and the dead could follow through if it's open. It also flattens the choice of building, because every home has the same foolproof safe room. Opinion: fixing it makes boarding, bracing and the choice of building matter.
findings.suggestion: Stage 1 (S): a zombie chasing you doesn't lose you when you go up to the roof. It walks to the top storey's stairwell cell and waits there, banging (noise). The status changes to 'ติดอยู่บนดาดฟ้า · ข้างล่างมีตัวรออยู่ N ตัว'. The roof becomes a pause and a decision point (wait for rain to cover your sound, jump down with the existing sprain risk, call a friend), not a win. Stage 2 (M, after playtesting stage 1): a roof door per stairwell as a Things kind 'roofdoor' on the top storey (Things already supports storey), with closed/boards/hp like a door. If it breaks, zombies can step out onto the roof (World.slide already has a roof mode, used by players). A roof you've barred is a real last stand.
findings.scope_check: Uses existing views and poses (zombies walk and bang as now). Stage 1 is AI state only. Stage 2 adds one small drawn hatch/door (static, redrawn only on state change). No GEN bump if the roof door is placed after the stoves (at the end of city generation), like place_stoves.

findings.title: Every shophouse is the same self-sufficient home, so there's nothing to choose
findings.observation: 11 of 12 shophouse plans share the same back half: tap T, gas stove G, water jar J, squat toilet q, back door B, fridge f, food cupboard F, and two full-length beds upstairs. Only the minimart differs (no stove, no beds, no floor 2). 70% of them get a working tap. Every G becomes a stove with 2-6 goes of gas. Every building has its own roof tank that starts with up to 24 sips. The shop front and the loot table are the only differences.
findings.evidence: Counted in data/prefabs/*.txt (barber, bikeshop, clinic, eatery, goldshop, hardware, home, massage, pharmacy, phoneshop, silkshop: G=1 T=1 J=1 q=1 B=1 f=1, 2 double-row beds on floor 2); things.gd:439-441 (tap 70%), 36 + 141-144 (gas 2-6), 461-464 (a stove on every G); buildings.gd:28-34; ROADMAP 'หาความสนุก' (line 385) already says 'ของมีทุกบ้าน'.
findings.why: 'Choosing where to live' is the promise of the game (ROADMAP line 3). When the house next door has the same bed, stove, tap and tank, the best home is the nearest closed one, and hunting for a better one never pays. That explains 'it's OK, but something's off': the home works, but you never have to think about it.
findings.suggestion: Give each building a few traits rolled from its existing seed inside Buildings.start (worked out at runtime; WorldState stores only changes, so no GEN bump): tank = none (25%) / cracked (drains to 0 over ~2 days) / small / big; gas bottle under the stove yes/no (50%: a stove without a bottle is cold); jar count 0-3 (see L4); upper-floor window grilles (safer, no escape); shutter left up at the outbreak (rec.open already 50%). Make the per-sign plans differ more at the back: the eatery has 2 gas bottles and a big pot, the hardware shop has padlocks and a ladder, the pharmacy has one bed. Things also run down: the stove's bottle runs out, a cracked tank empties. Show all of it in the appraisal line (L5).
findings.scope_check: Data and systems (Buildings.start, Things state) with no new views. Art is limited to small states on existing props: stove with or without a bottle, tank drawn cracked. Nothing per frame. Changing prefab rows would need a GEN bump, so do the traits first; they don't.

findings.title: Water never runs out and the rain falls into the wrong container
findings.observation: Rain lasts 90-200 s and, on average, comes every ~13-16 real minutes (dry spells of 150-400 s, with a 30% (day) or 45% (night) chance of rain at the end of each). TANK_RAIN is 12 sips per game hour, and rain time is counted in game seconds, so one ~145 s shower (14.5 game hours) pours ~170 sips into a 60-sip tank. A survivor drinks ~2.2 sips a game day (100 thirst per 720 s, 15 thirst per sip). So every shophouse tank can supply about 6 people indefinitely (my arithmetic from the constants). The water jar J is decoration only. In real Bangkok, rooftop tanks are filled from the mains by a pump, not by rain. Rain is caught in โอ่ง under the eaves.
findings.evidence: survival.gd:30-36; buildings.gd:20-22, 68-74; main.gd:554 (rain_total += delta * time_speed); survival.gd:13-14 (THIRST_RATE); items.gd:511-515 (LIQUIDS: tap sip 15, sick 0.06); city_gen.gd:62-65 (J = decor 'jar' in DECOR_BLOCKS); ROADMAP line 343 ('ประปาหยุด (ต้องมีแท็งก์/รองน้ำฝน/อยู่ใกล้คลอง)'). Reference: Project Zomboid shuts water and power off at a random point in the first ~30 days, and the fixtures then hold only what's left; rain collectors are how you replace it (mobalytics.gg/gamebase/guides/project-zomboid-water-power-shut-off; pzwiki.net/wiki/Plumbing).
findings.why: In a Thai-city apocalypse, water is the most realistic and universal reason to choose a home or to move. At the moment it never runs out anywhere, so nothing pushes the core loop (go out, come home, use things). Fact: the constants. Opinion: water should be the main thing you size up when you look at a house.
findings.suggestion: Three sources with different trade-offs. (1) Mains, on a world-day curve (ROADMAP 'โลกเปลี่ยนตามวัน'): days 1-7 taps run and top the tanks up; days 8-14 a trickle a few hours a day; then dry. It's a single factor inside Buildings.tank. (2) The roof tank is only what's stored: no rain, or TANK_RAIN ~1-2 as roof run-off. Big buildings keep the cistern + generator pump, so water costs fuel trips. (3) Jars: make J a Things kind 'jar' (placed from decor like place_stoves, appended last so existing ids stay the same) holding ~30 sips. It fills from rain_total only while its lid is off; you drink from it with a bowl (ขัน) or fill a bottle; an open jar breeds mosquitoes (L8). The canal stays unlimited, but 45% sick, so boil. Then the choice becomes: a house with jars and a big tank, near the canal, or a flat whose cistern needs fuel.
findings.scope_check: Uses existing views and the existing Things/Buildings/WorldState. The only art is the jar lid on/off (the jar is already drawn). Timestamp state, nothing per frame. No GEN bump (placement comes from existing decor).

findings.title: Different building types should be different lives, and the game should tell you what a place offers
findings.observation: The types exist: shophouse (12 plans), minimart, and big buildings (flats, office, hospital, mall, market) of 3-7 storeys with 2-14 trapped zombies. Generator, cistern and pump exist only in big buildings. A temple refugee camp is planned. But nothing tells the player what a building offers: the E prompt at a front door just says 'ประตู'.
findings.evidence: big_plans.gd:14-20 (KINDS), 131-150 (roles); buildings.gd:23-46; things.gd:445-449 (generators only where plans put Q); interact.gd:81-90 (door titles); ROADMAP 344 (condo rooms for several families), 357 and 378 (temple camp). Reference: State of Decay 2 makes every base's beds, water and power visible when you choose one (gosunoob.com/state-of-decay-2/home-bases-locations-best-base-outposts/).
findings.why: A choice needs trade-offs you can read. Without an appraisal, players can't compare houses even after L3/L4 make them differ.
findings.suggestion: Trade-off matrix. Shophouse: 2 entrances (loud shutter, quiet back door), 2 floors + roof, small tank, jars, gas stove, next to shops; ground floor exposed. Townhouse (a new plan kind with no shop: front yard gate + carport = an extra layer, bike parked inside, quieter soi): more privacy, fewer supplies. Flat/condo unit high up: stairs only (lifts dead), trapped zombies to clear first, water only via cistern + generator (fuel trips), sound fades per floor (L1), far from loot, no jumping out; neighbours for co-op. Office: glass, no beds or kitchen, generator; a daytime depot, not a home. Market/mall: not homes. Temple camp: safe and shared, no private storage, fire only in the common kitchen; where new players start. Implementation: an appraisal line read from Buildings/Things state, shown at an entrance, on first sleep and when claiming, e.g. 'ทางเข้า 2 · น้ำ: แท็งก์ 40/60 · โอ่ง 2 · แก๊สราว 3 ครั้ง · 2 ชั้น + ดาดฟ้า · ซอมบี้ในตึก 0'.
findings.scope_check: The appraisal is a read-only UI line (existing toast/prompt style, clean HUD). Townhouse is a new prefab text file (data; GEN bump when added). No new views; nothing per frame.

findings.title: Home life runs on a stopwatch
findings.observation: DAY_LENGTH 240 s, so a game hour is 10 real seconds. Boiling water takes 0.5 game hours = 5 real seconds; cooking rice 0.75 = 7.5 s. Cooked rice spoils after 30 game hours = 5 real minutes. Night is when time > 0.764 or < 0.036, about 27% of the day = ~65 real seconds. Sleeping speeds time up x6 only when every living player is asleep; with 20-50 players on a server I expect that never to happen (inference). A generator's full tank lasts 8 game hours = 80 s.
findings.evidence: main.gd:10-11; things.gd:33-34, 40; items.cfg [rice] spoil=30; main.gd:1071-1076 (light, night < 0.6); survival.gd:66-78 (NIGHT_SPEED, time_speed). The 4-minute day is already known from the city review; this lists what it does to home life.
findings.why: Core rule 9 ('world jobs you start and walk away from') and evening routines like 'cook, board up, sleep' need minutes to feel like living. At this scale a meal is a blink and a night is a coffee break. Every new home timer (lamp oil, jar filling, charcoal) inherits the problem.
findings.suggestion: Decide once, before adding new home timers. Either (a) lengthen the day (e.g. 20-24 real minutes) and rescale hunger and thirst so food and water last the same real time, or (b) keep 4-minute days but state home durations in real minutes (a Main.REAL_MIN constant used by Things/Buildings: boiling ~1 real minute, rice ~2, cooked rice keeps ~1 real hour, a candle ~3). Online, sleep can't fast-forward the world, so make sleep a fast-forward for your own body only (needs slower, healing faster; partly there already) and switch off the x6 world speed on shared servers. Check with the 20-minute new-player test (ROADMAP 394).
findings.scope_check: Constants plus test updates only; no views or art. Tests that assume game-hour timings must change, so do it as its own round.

findings.title: You have no light of your own at home, and a lit home can't give you away
findings.observation: At night indoors you only have night_eyes (a few metres around you) or a headlamp whose batteries run down. Room bulbs light only with generator power. Zombies see further in lit places. There are no candles, lanterns or oil lamps in items.cfg (only lighter, matches, battery, powerbank). h06: asleep at night, the bedroom is lit only by your own night-eyes glow.
findings.evidence: player.gd:164, 798; survival.gd:434-447 (_tick_lamp); world.gd:480-499 (_bulb_on, is_lit, light_spots); zombie.gd:520; items.cfg sections [battery] [lighter] [matches]; screenshot h06_asleep_night_z5.
findings.why: Light at night is the clearest 'someone lives here' sign in a dead city and a classic choice: light (work, see what's in the room) vs dark (hidden). It collides with batteries, fire, boards, curtains, windows and zombie sight, which is the 'few systems, many collisions' rule.
findings.suggestion: Items: candle (เทียน: homes, shrines, minimarts; burns a few real minutes), oil lamp (ตะเกียง: fuel from a jerrycan), battery lantern. Put one down with F (the trap-placing path) as a Things kind 'lamp' with storey and a burn-until timestamp. A lit lamp adds a light_spots entry (is_lit already reads that list) and lights the building's windows through the existing BuildingProp 'lit' glow. The leak: at night, a lit building whose outer openings aren't boarded or curtained is a slow 'sight' lure; every few seconds, zombies outside within ~150 px that can see its front go to investigate (a stimulus kind 'sight' that rain doesn't reduce). What light gives you: crafting, repairs and bandaging at normal speed (x1.5 slower in the dark), zombies in the room visible, and it counts toward sleep comfort (L8). Curtains (decor 'C') and boards block the leak.
findings.scope_check: No new views. Small static art (candle/lantern, like other things). PointLight2D per lamp: cap it at a few per building and measure with F3. The lure check runs every few seconds on the server, not per frame.

findings.title: Heat, sleep and comfort as a few conditions, not meters
findings.observation: Heat comes only from clothing. Stand fans are decoration only; the 'fan' item can only be taken apart for scrap. Shutting a building tight has no downside. Sleep only heals (x3 if safe, x1.5 in a bed, x0.4 near a rotting body), and nothing lasts after you wake. The mongkol already turns belief into a small real effect. Spirit houses stand on the sois; Buddha shelves and altars are decoration. Jars and tyres (standing water) are decoration.
findings.evidence: player.gd:424-428 (heat() = clothes only); survival.gd:217 (sweat), 60-67 and 145-169 (sleep heal), 238 (wear_mult 'stamina'); city_gen.gd:62 (n = fan decor), items.cfg [fan] (salvage only); city_gen.gd:1038, 1053 (spirit houses); screenshots h05, h06 (fan beside the bed), h01 (spirit house). Reference: This War of Mine makes heating and beds shelter decisions, and boarding holes keeps out both cold and raiders (gamefaqs.gamespot.com/pc/771423-this-war-of-mine/faqs/70840/our-shelter).
findings.why: The real Bangkok trade-off is air vs safety: people sleep with windows open and a fan on, and a sealed shophouse in April is an oven. Heat is the natural counterweight to L1 (open lets sound out; shut is hot), and it gives power and batteries a daily use at home. Carrying 'slept well' out on the next run ties home to the core loop without a new bar.
findings.suggestion: Add these as data in Body.CONDITIONS. 'อบอ้าว': in a shut building by day (06-18) or asleep in one, unless a fan runs (the fan item placed with batteries or building power), an upper-floor opening is open (needs L11), or it's raining; effects thirst x1.4, stamina_regen x0.85, sleep heal x0.7. 'นอนเต็มอิ่ม': on waking after 6+ game hours asleep, safe and in a bed, stamina_regen x1.2 for about 8 hours. 'นอนไม่พอ': woken early or slept outside, x0.85. 'ยุงกัด': asleep near an open jar or tyres with no net or coil gives a small chance of 'ไข้เลือดออก' a day later (fever 2-3 days, speed x0.9, tiny damage); items: net (มุ้ง, put on a bed) and mosquito coil (ยากันยุง, faint smell). 'ใจสงบ': ไหว้ at a spirit house with an offering (น้ำแดง, พวงมาลัย, ธูป found in homes and minimarts), once a day, stamina_regen x1.1. NOT: a temperature simulation, air conditioning, a tiredness/bladder/hygiene meter, or a morale bar.
findings.scope_check: Data rows plus small checks in _tick_sleep and _tick_needs. Existing poses (sleep, stand); the ไหว้ gesture could be a small arm pose through the rig in the existing views (optional; a toast works). No per-frame drawing; checks every second.

findings.title: Security is all or nothing and anonymous: no locks, and the shutter opens from the street
findings.observation: Doors and shutters open for anyone from either side. City generation even notes shutters are 'padlocked from inside', but that isn't modelled. Boards are the only way to secure anything. ROADMAP phase 2 lists locks + crowbar prying and furniture dragging.
findings.evidence: doors.gd:98-121 (_toggle_door), 147-159 (_toggle_shutter: no side or lock check); city_gen.gd:531-533 (comment 'padlocked from inside'; rec.open 50%); doors.gd:64-95 (boards); ROADMAP lines 197-198.
findings.why: Pulling the shutter down and padlocking the grille when you leave is the everyday ritual of a Thai home. Online it's also the physical form of claiming a home. With boards as the only tool, every secured home looks and plays the same.
findings.suggestion: Padlock item (hardware shop and homes, common). Used on a shutter or door from inside, it can't be opened from the street. Used from outside as you leave (you keep the key), it stays locked while you're away and is visible to others: the sign that someone lives here. Prying it open with a crowbar or pipe is slow and loud (NOISE_BREAK), a choice players make; zombies still only bash. Bracing: E on a door next to existing furniture in the same room, 'ดันตู้ขวางประตู'. The door gets a 'braced' state (+hp like 2 boards, can't be opened from either side until you pull it back, loud to push), and the piece is drawn in the doorway. Why this is NOT base building: nothing new is created, no cell changes type, only furniture already in that room can be used, and it's a state on an existing door, not free placement. Free dragging anywhere would be base building in practice (walls of fridges, blocked streets, pathing exploits) and should stay out.
findings.scope_check: Uses existing doors, furniture and views. Small art: a padlock on the shutter, furniture drawn in the doorway. The door record gets 'locked' and 'braced' fields (the old door save path; move it into WorldState when touched). Nothing per frame.

findings.title: Cooking is free and silent: one gas stove per kitchen, no other way to cook
findings.observation: Every kitchen G becomes a stove with 2-6 goes of gas. Cooking gives off a 110 px smell. Stripping furniture gives plenty of wood, but wood is only used for boards. Instant noodles are eaten dry (drink -5).
findings.evidence: things.gd:25, 33-36, 99-113, 238-249, 461-464; furniture_prop.gd:14-19 (STRIP gives wood); items.cfg [mama] drink=-5.0, [rice_raw] cooks.
findings.why: In a Thai home, cooking fuel is the heavy gas bottle (swapped and delivered) and the charcoal stove (เตาถ่าน/อั้งโล่) of street vendors and older homes. Scarce gas plus smoky charcoal gives a daily choice (quiet but scarce vs plentiful but smoky) that collides with stimulus, furniture stripping, the roof and the walls (L1).
findings.suggestion: The gas bottle becomes a heavy carryable item (ถังแก๊ส, ~15 kg: slows you) that sits under a stove; a stove without one is cold (L3); eateries have two. Add a charcoal stove as a Things kind (found in eateries and the market, or carried as an item and set down with F) that burns charcoal or wood. Its smoke is a smell twice as strong as gas cooking, plus a visible smoke column (reuse the smoke drawn for burning corpses). Used inside a shut building, it gives a 'สำลักควัน' condition (stamina, coughing = small noise). So you cook by the back door or on the roof. Recipe: instant noodles + boiled water = 'มาม่าต้ม' (more food, no thirst hit).
findings.scope_check: Things kind + items + a condition (data). Reuses the corpse-burning smoke art. Existing views (a standing player cooks as now). Server stimulus every 5 s like the stove. No GEN bump (the charcoal stove is placed or found, not generated).

findings.title: A flat or condo unit can't be a home: no doors upstairs, copy-paste units
findings.observation: Upper storeys turn every wall, window and door letter into solid wall, and 'Doorways up here are open'. So above ground there's no unit door and no window you can open. For a flats block, spot_safe needs every ground-floor opening shut (3 front doors, 2 fire doors, a lobby front of windows, each 60% a window, and every ground-floor unit door) and no zombie anywhere inside. The unit template puts bed, fridge, sink, tap and squat toilet in one open room. h09/h10: 10 identical units per floor, the toilet beside the bed. Every fridge, home or shop, is drawn as a glass-door drinks cooler (h03 kitchen, h09 each unit, 21 nurse station).
findings.evidence: city_gen.gd:436-450 (_build_storey); city_gen.gd:509-510; big_plans.gd:98-108, 231-243 ('unit'); survival.gd:91-104; furniture_prop.gd:139-145 ('fridge' draw); screenshots h09_flats_storey3_z2_5, h10_flats_room_z4, h03_back_kitchen_z5; ROADMAP 344.
findings.why: Living high up (safe, far from supplies, water pumped) is one of the most Bangkok choices, and the online plan needs many households per building. Without a door per unit it can't happen. The identical open-plan units read as a hospital ward, not somebody's room.
findings.suggestion: Enabler (L): doors on upper storeys, i.e. door records with a storey, door_at per storey, DoorProp drawn on its own floor like furniture, and zombies banging per storey (they already move per storey). Then a new unit plan: steel grille + wooden door; a bathroom behind its own door (q + T + a small jar); a balcony strip at the back with a door (air, laundry, rain jar); household fridge. Appraisal and spot_safe per unit (the room map is already built in city_gen). Now, as an S step: a household fridge variant (white, 1-2 doors) for fridges in homes. The unit plans need a GEN bump; ship them with the online housing round.
findings.scope_check: No character views. Door art exists and is reused per floor, drawn only on the floor you're on (the multi-floor rule 'draw one floor at a time'). Networking of door state per storey. The fridge variant is static art. GEN bump for the unit plans.

findings.title: Make the home yours and make it matter: claim, attention, co-op
findings.observation: Claiming today is one field: any bed anywhere can be set as your respawn. Buildings has an 'owner' field that nothing uses. Horde zombies spawn around a random living player, not around homes. Only the 'cook' and 'board' quests involve the home.
findings.evidence: actions.gd:405-406, interact.gd:198-204; buildings.gd:13, 34; survival.gd:389-400; quests.cfg ([intro_board], [daily_cook], [daily_fortify]); ROADMAP 339-346 (spray paint, lockable cupboards, 1 home per person/group, 7-day abandon, 'คืนฝูงบุกมุ่งไปบ้านที่มีคน'). Reference: in This War of Mine, night raids hit the shelter itself and boarded holes plus a reinforced door lower the risk (same gamefaqs page).
findings.why: A home only matters if it's visibly yours and something comes for it. This is where the living systems feed the core loop and co-op.
findings.suggestion: Claiming is one act with three visible parts: spray paint on the front door or shutter (a decal in the group's colour), claimed bed(s) for respawn, and up to 2 lockable cupboards (locked to owner or group; prying is slow and loud). Buildings.owner + 'since'. 'Attention' grows with days lived there and noise leaked (L1). Horde nights split their spawns: some around players as now, some at occupied homes' outer openings, so your boards and braces are tested even while you're away. Locked cupboards keep their loot, but a broken door lets zombies in and you come home to clear them. Co-op: a group claims one home; roles come out of the systems (the cook with the gas bottle, the medic, the runner with the bike, the lookout on the roof), not role classes. Quests: new objective types 'stash' (N food/water in your home's containers), 'sleep_safe', and a daily 'เติมโอ่ง'.
findings.scope_check: Systems and online data (the ROADMAP database plan already lists claimed home + locked cupboards). The only art is the spray decal on existing door props. Horde spawn logic is server-side only. No views.

findings.title: Bring the bike inside at night
findings.observation: Bikes can't cross FLOOR or DOOR tiles: riding uses World.slide with road=true, which refuses those tiles. Yet the 'home' plan's own comment says 'the bike inside' and puts a parked-bike decoration 'e' in the front room. A bike left outside stays where you parked it, and online others can hotwire it.
findings.evidence: world.gd:882-889 (can_stand: road and tile in [FLOOR, DOOR]); vehicles.gd:112; data/prefabs/home.txt line 1 comment + row 'We.jRW' (e = bike decor, city_gen.gd:62); vehicles.gd:16, 20 (HOTWIRE_TIME, KEY_CHANCE).
findings.why: Every Thai family wheels the moped into the front room before pulling the shutter down. It ties the vehicle to the home, protects it (online), and uses the shutter's wide opening. It's also a realistic reason to pick a shophouse over a flat.
findings.suggestion: 'Push' mode: E on your stopped bike near an open shutter or door wheels it at walking speed, engine off, no noise. While pushed, the road check allows FLOOR/DOOR tiles when the doorway is 2+ cells wide (shutters). Park it on the ground floor. Pose: the walking pose with hands on the rig's existing handlebar anchors, in the existing views. Inside, behind a padlocked shutter (L9), nobody can take it. Keep the rule that generation never parks bikes in shop fronts; this is only for players.
findings.scope_check: No new views. The pose goes through the rig using existing hand anchors, so clothes follow. Bike art reused. One more collision flag in the vehicle step; nothing extra per frame.

findings.title: Staged plan: 4 rounds, each playable
findings.observation: The ROADMAP asks for 'one round at a time, each playable, with tests' and 'core loop first'. Phase 2 is done when 'you can live in one house for several days using only what's in it and around it'.
findings.evidence: ROADMAP 192-203 (phase 2), 292-299 (long-term principles), 383-394 ('หาความสนุก').
findings.why: Doing the walls first makes every later supply collide with them; doing supplies before claiming makes the claim worth something.
findings.suggestion: Round 0 (S): decide the clock scale (L6). Round 1 'Walls and roof' (S-M, no GEN bump): L1 (outer openings count, walls muffle sound, per-floor falloff), L2 stage 1 (roof siege), the L5 appraisal line, household fridge art, the 'rested' condition. Playable: shutting your house clearly quiets you, horde night besieges your house, and you can see why one house beats another. Round 2 'Supplies differ and run down' (M): L3 traits, L4 water (mains by day, no-rain tank, jar Thing), L10 gas bottle + charcoal smoke. Playable: you pick a house for its jars, tank and gas, and move when they run out. Round 3 'Nights at home' (M): L7 lamps + window glow, L8 heat/fan/mosquitoes/spirit house, L9 padlock + bracing, B1 bike inside. Playable: an evening routine (light or dark, open or shut, lock up, bike in). Round 4 'Home online' (L): L12 claiming, horde at homes, group home, L11 upper-floor doors and condo units, temple camp as the start. Playable: 20-50 players each with a home you can recognise. Keep out of every round: base building, free furniture dragging, need meters beyond hunger/thirst, morale bars, decorating, new character views.
findings.scope_check: Each round changes data and systems, plus small static props on existing views. Only round 4 needs a GEN bump (unit plans, townhouse). Measure with F3 after round 3 (lamp lights).

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. main.gd:673-684: stimulus() applies only rain (sound x0.65, smell x0.4) and a flat OTHER_FLOOR 0.5. It never checks walls or doors. survival.gd:91-104: spot_safe fails on any open or broken door whose cell is in the building rect, and on any zombie in the building on ANY storey (z.storey is not checked). city_gen.gd:505-508 generates every 'd' door open. All 11 non-minimart plans share the rows 'WG.dqW' and 'WWdWWW', so every shophouse starts with two open interior doors on the ground floor. Hammering is NOISE_SWING 90 (doors.gd:92, main.gd:66) and the shutter is NOISE_HIT 130 (doors.gd:159). This also matters in play: a zombie that goes to investigate a sound paths to it and bashes closed doors in the way (zombie.gd:445-457, 473-478). So noise leaking out of a house turns into door-bashing.
verdicts.reason: The facts are right and the fix is cheap. It is the hinge that the light, heat, cooking and generator systems all need to collide with. ROADMAP core 4 already names 'ผนังกั้น' and core 6 names 'ปิดแน่นไหม'; neither is built. Start with a simple yes/no 'sealed' flag; the three-level shell can come later.
verdicts.revised_observation: Walls and doors change nothing for zombies' senses. The 'safe' check also counts interior doors that the game generates open, plus zombies on any floor. So a shut home is just a sleep-bonus switch, and it fails for reasons the player can't see.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: (1) spot_safe: count only openings on the border of the building rect, and ignore interior 'd' doors. In big buildings, count only zombies on your storey ±1. (2) Keep a per-building 'sealed' bool (every border opening closed and not broken). Recompute it in World.set_door, for that door's building only. (3) In stimulus: when the source and the zombie are not in the same building and the building in between is sealed, radius *= 0.5. Boarded windows and a lowered shutter can be a later refinement. (4) Replace the flat 0.5 with radius * 0.5^|storey difference|. (5) Add one status line when the building is sealed. No GEN bump, no save change.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. zombie.gd:174, 189, 202 and 515 all skip on_roof players. You reach the roof by going 'up' past the top storey, which sets storey 0 (actions.gd:283-288). The status and toast both say zombies can't come up (body.gd:328-329, actions.gd:298). h08 shows a '↓บันได' hatch on every roof. The lens missed two things that make it stronger. First, from a roof you can throw and shoot at street zombies, and they can't reach you (combat.gd:104-111, 629-641). Second, a row's roofs are joined, and from any roof you can take any building's stairs down (interact.gd:42-44, actions.gd:289-292), so a boarded home can be entered from a neighbour's roof.
verdicts.reason: The finding is right and matters most on horde nights. But ROADMAP line 393 lists 'หนี (รถ หลังคา คลอง)', so the roof is an intended escape. The fix must keep it an escape and make it a pause, not a win. Car roofs already work the way roofs should: _nearest_player doesn't skip on_car players, so zombies crowd around the car without reaching you.
verdicts.revised_observation: Going up to the roof makes you vanish for every zombie, and it becomes a firing perch with no risk. A siege at home is always solved by 'go up'.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Stage 1 (M): for a zombie that is already chasing you, treat the roof as one floor above the top storey. _stairs_after brings it up to the top storey's stairwell, where it waits and bangs (NOISE_HIT every few seconds). After 1-2 game hours without seeing you, it gives up. Status line: 'ติดอยู่บนดาดฟ้า · มีตัวรออยู่ที่บันได N ตัว'. Ways out stay open: walk along the row and go down another building's stairs, jump (sprain risk), or wait. Stage 2 (after playtesting): make the hatch that is already drawn on every roof closable and boardable. Make it a Things kind at the roof, added at the end of generation like place_stoves, so no GEN bump. This also closes the neighbour's-roof way into boarded homes.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed by counting data/prefabs. The first six rows ('WWBWWW WT.WJW WG.dqW WK.WWW Wf..FW WWdWWW') are the same in 11 of 12 plans; only the minimart differs. Each of those 11 has G, T, J, q, B, f, F and K once, and 4 'b' on floor 2, which makes two full-length beds. The eatery has 2 fridges. Tap chance is 70% (things.gd:440). Gas is 2-6 goes (things.gd:36, 141-144). Every G gets a stove (things.gd:461-464). Tanks start with 0-24 sips (buildings.gd:22, 32). ROADMAP line 385 already names 'ของมีทุกบ้าน' as a gap in the fun.
verdicts.reason: This is a real root cause. Two corrections. 'No tank 25%' is unrealistic, since nearly every Bangkok shophouse has a tank; vary its size or state instead. And changing Buildings.start also changes the defaults of every untouched building in existing saves. That's acceptable, but it should be said.
verdicts.revised_observation: Eleven of twelve shophouse plans have the same back half, and the runtime state (tap, gas, tank) is rolled from the same narrow ranges. So the best home is simply the nearest one that's shut.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Runtime traits from rec.seed, with no GEN bump: gas bottle under the stove 50% (a stove with no bottle is cold; the eatery gets 2); tank small, normal or big, with 20% 'leaking' (it drains on the clock, using the same timestamp maths as rain); jar count, see L4. Later, batched with other generation changes that need a GEN bump: make the back halves differ by sign (eatery: two stoves and a big pot; hardware: ladder and padlocks; pharmacy: one bed; some homes with the kitchen out in a back yard). Show what the player has learned through L5.

verdicts.fact_check: The arithmetic is right. A game hour is 10 s (main.gd:11). TANK_RAIN is 12 per hour (buildings.gd:21). rain_total counts game seconds (main.gd:554). A shower lasts 90-200 real seconds (survival.gd:36), which puts 108-240 sips into a 60-sip tank. Thirst is 100 per 720 s and a tap sip is 15, so a survivor drinks about 2.2 sips per game day. The jar 'J' is decoration only (city_gen.gd:63, 67). Part of the root cause is the clock: weather timers run in real seconds against a 240-second day, so one shower lasts 9-20 game hours. Also, rain filling the rooftop tank is an AGREED design: ROADMAP line 125, core 6, 'แท็งก์น้ำบนดาดฟ้า (ฝนเติม ...)', agreed 2026-09-27.
verdicts.reason: Water that never runs out is a real problem, and ROADMAP lines 343 and 390 already plan water that stops. But 'no rain into the tank' reverses an agreed decision. Tuning the rate down gives the same scarcity and stays within it.
verdicts.revised_observation: One shower more than refills every rooftop tank, because TANK_RAIN is high and a shower lasts half a game day. So tap water never runs out, and the jar is only decoration.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Keep rain filling the tank, as agreed, but make it a trickle: TANK_RAIN 12 → about 1-2, one data line, so a shower gives roughly 15-30 sips. Add mains water by world day (ROADMAP 390) as the reason taps run early on; it is one factor inside Buildings.tank. Make the jar a Things kind created from the existing 'J' decor, appended last like place_stoves so no GEN bump. It fills from rain_total while its lid is off; this is the 'รองน้ำฝน' in line 343. The canal stays as it is. Re-tune after the clock decision (L6).

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. KINDS are at big_plans.gd:14-20. Generators exist only where a plan puts Q (things.gd:448-449). A door's E title is just 'ประตู' or 'ประตูเหล็กม้วน' (interact.gd:85). One gap: flats and offices have no stove at all (see missed item M2), so the matrix overstates flats as a home.
verdicts.reason: Making the differences readable is right. But the proposed line is an x-ray: tank level and 'ซอมบี้ในตึก 0' seen from the front door. That kills the tension of scouting and isn't realistic. The townhouse needs new plot shapes (yard, carport), which means city-generation work and a GEN bump (L effort), so defer it. The type matrix is a design note, not a task.
verdicts.revised_observation: Buildings will differ once L3 and L4 land, but the game gives no way to remember or compare what you found in each one.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Show a 'what I know about this place' line that holds only what this player has seen. Tank level is known after using a tap or seeing the roof tank, gas after looking at the stove, entrances after seeing them. Store it per player, like map pins or quests. Show it on sleeping, on claiming a bed, and on the map at your home. Leave the building-type matrix as a design note. Add the next building type only when its plot shape is already supported.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. DAY_LENGTH is 240 and HOUR is 10 s (main.gd:10-11). Boiling is 0.5 h = 5 s and rice 0.75 h = 7.5 s (things.gd:33-34). Cooked rice spoils in 30 h = 5 minutes (items.cfg [rice]). Night is when light < 0.6, i.e. t > 0.764 or t < 0.036, about 65 s (main.gd:1071-1076). The x6 NIGHT_SPEED happens only when every living named player is asleep (survival.gd:71-78). A generator's tank lasts 8 h = 80 s. The 4-minute day was already known from the city review; this finding adds what it does to home life. It also explains L4: a shower lasts 9-20 game hours.
verdicts.reason: This is the right prerequisite, and nearly every home timer inherits the problem. Option (b), real-minute durations under a 4-minute day, makes the game say contradictory things ('rice ready in 6 game hours', a 14-hour shower). Prefer (a).
verdicts.revised_observation: The 4-minute day makes every home job a few seconds long, a night about a minute, and a shower half a day. Sleep can't skip time online.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Settle it in one round. Choose a day length (for example 20-24 real minutes). Decide whether 'food for 5 days' means 5 game days or should shrink (ROADMAP 392 already tries 2-3 days). Convert the weather timers to game hours. List everything that moves with the change: horde every 3 days, corpse rot, generator fuel, skill EXP pacing, tests. On shared servers, drop the x6 skip and make sleep a fast-forward for your own body only (slower needs, faster healing), which is mostly there already. Then re-run the 20-minute new-player test.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. items.cfg has lighter, matches, battery, powerbank and headlamp, but no candle, lantern or flashlight. is_lit reads light_spots and needs power for room bulbs (world.gd:489-499). Zombies see further when you are lit (zombie.gd:520). night_eyes is for the local player only (player.gd:164). In h06 the bedroom at night is lit only by the player's own glow.
verdicts.reason: It's a good collision (light against being seen), and ROADMAP line 92 ('ในตึกมืดถ้าไม่มีไฟ') and line 196 (light switch) point the same way. It needs L1 first, so that light leaking through open windows means something, and L6. The 'x1.5 slower in the dark' rule for crafting touches many actions; drop it for now.
verdicts.revised_observation: At home at night the only light is a headlamp or the generator, and a lit room is never seen from outside unless the generator is running.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Add candle and lantern items. Put one down with F as a Things 'lamp' with a storey and a burn-until timestamp. A lit lamp adds a light_spots entry and turns on that building's window glow. Every 5 s the server checks each building with a lit lamp: if its border windows aren't boarded or curtained, it sends a 'sight' stimulus outward, which rain doesn't reduce. Cap it at 2 PointLight2D per building and measure with F3 on web.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. heat() comes from clothes only (player.gd:424-428). The fan decor 'n' is decoration, and the [fan] item can only be salvaged (items.cfg 2203-2211). Sleep heals x3 when safe, x1.5 in a bed, x0.4 near a rotting body (survival.gd:60-62, 166-167), and nothing carries over after waking. Body.CONDITIONS supports mods (body.gd:39-76).
verdicts.reason: 'Rested' is a cheap, direct link from home to the next run. 'Stuffy' is realistic, but it punishes shutting up, which horde nights require, so keep it mild. Mosquitoes and dengue need L4's jars plus new items. ไหว้ศาลพระภูมิ is already planned (ROADMAP 195), and body temperature is listed as unplanned (301). Too much for one round.
verdicts.revised_observation: Sleep only heals and has no after-effect. The home's air (open or shut, fan) has no effect at all.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Now, as data (S): 'นอนเต็มอิ่ม' after 6+ game hours asleep, safe and in a bed, giving stamina_regen x1.15 for about 8 game hours; 'นอนไม่พอ' when woken early. Later (M): 'อบอ้าว' by day in a sealed building with no fan, no open window and no rain, giving thirst x1.2 only. Much later: mosquitoes from open jars, and the planned ไหว้ศาลพระภูมิ as a small daily buff shown with a toast (a rig pose is optional).

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. _toggle_door and _toggle_shutter have no side or lock check (doors.gd:98-121, 147-159). The 'padlocked from inside' comment (city_gen.gd:531-532) isn't modelled. Boards are the only way to secure anything (doors.gd:64-95). ROADMAP lines 197-198 plan both 'ลากเฟอร์นิเจอร์' and 'กุญแจ: ล็อกประตู, งัดด้วยชะแลง'.
verdicts.reason: Two clauses clash with the ROADMAP. 'Free dragging should stay out' contradicts the planned 'ลากเฟอร์นิเจอร์' (line 197). Padlocking other players out contradicts line 341 ('คนอื่นเดินเข้าได้แต่เปิดตู้ไม่ได้'). A padlock also does nothing against zombies, which never open doors, only bash them (zombie.gd:445-457). So its value is online only, and there the ROADMAP already chose lockable cupboards. Bracing is the part that matters against zombies.
verdicts.revised_observation: Securing a home means boards only: every secured house looks and plays the same. The planned locks and furniture dragging aren't built yet.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Build bracing first, as a bounded first step of the planned furniture dragging. E on a door or shutter with a searchable piece of furniture in the same room gives the door a 'braced' state: +hp like 2 boards, it can't be opened until pulled back, and moving the piece is loud. Draw that piece in the doorway. Whether full dragging comes later is the user's call; point out its costs (blocked streets, pathing) rather than ruling it out. Padlocks come with online claiming, in a way that fits line 341 (a visible 'occupied' sign, or a lock only while the owner is inside).

verdicts.fact_check: The title is wrong. Cooking is neither free nor silent: each stove has 2-6 goes, then says 'แก๊สหมดแล้ว' (things.gd:36, 108, 141-144), and gives off a 110-px smell every 5 s (things.gd:35, 353-354), as the observation itself says. What's true: every shophouse has a stove, so across the city gas is effectively unlimited. Wood is used only for boards (furniture_prop.gd:14-19), and mama gives drink -5 (items.cfg). The lens missed that flats and offices have no stove at all (big_plans.gd:236-247; 'G' appears only in mall 'food' units, line 399), so anyone living high up can't boil water.
verdicts.reason: The scarcity half is already covered by L3's gas-bottle trait. The charcoal stove's real value is as a portable stove that makes flats and roofs liveable. It is also the natural first piece of the planned fire system (ROADMAP 199, core 8).
verdicts.revised_observation: Gas is never scarce because every shophouse has a stove with a few goes, and there's only one way to cook. In flats and offices there's no way to cook or boil at all.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: (1) S: gas bottle present or absent per stove (L3). (2) S: add a 'มาม่าต้ม' recipe (mama + boiled water) in data. (3) M: a charcoal stove as a carried item, set down with F, working as a stove variant that burns wood or charcoal. It gives a stronger smell, reuses the corpse-burning smoke art, and gives a 'ควัน' condition inside a sealed building. The 15-kg carryable gas bottle can come later.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. On upper storeys W, w, U, D and B become IWALL and 'd' becomes open floor (city_gen.gd:436-453). The unit template puts bed, cabinet, TV, fan, fridge, sink, tap and squat toilet in one room, with no stove (big_plans.gd:236-247). Every fridge is drawn as a glass-door drinks cooler with coloured bottles and a blue base (furniture_prop.gd:139-145), in the home kitchen in h03 and in every flat unit in h09. h09 and h10 show about 10 identical units per floor with open doorways.
verdicts.reason: It's correct, but it mixes a cheap realism fix with a large engine change. The household fridge shows in every kitchen today and needs only one draw branch, so it should be its own quick item. Doors on upper storeys are L effort and belong with the online housing round (ROADMAP 344).
verdicts.revised_observation: Home fridges are drawn as shop drinks coolers. Flat units are identical open rooms with no door, no kitchen and the toilet beside the bed.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Now (S): in FurnitureProp, draw 'fridge' as a white household fridge (solid door, handle) when data.table is 'home' or the room is a unit; keep the glass cooler for shops and minimarts. Later (L, with online housing): door records with a storey and door_at per storey, and a new unit plan with its own door, a bathroom behind a door, a balcony and a small stove (GEN bump).
